Michael Saylor expects bank lending and a upcoming wave of BTC-backed credit products to drive Bitcoin's next bull market.

Speaking at the Cantor Convergence conference, the Strategy chairman outlined how expanding access to financing could increase Bitcoin purchases, discourage existing holders from selling and attract institutional capital.

“Bank credit is going to be the key driver of additional buying and the key driver for the not selling.”.

His outlook rests on two related developments: Strategy's efforts to raise billions through digital-credit securities and growing interest among traditional banks in accepting Bitcoin-related investments as collateral.

Saylor expects both channels to strengthen demand for Bitcoin, although their ability to sustain purchases during market downturns remains uncertain.

Saylor stated Strategy could significantly expand its Bitcoin accumulation program by issuing additional digital-credit instruments, building on a financing business he estimated had helped create a $16 billion market in 21 months.

“The company has right now the capacity to sell 48 billion of this stuff without Bitcoin price moving.”.

Strategy's model involves raising capital through preferred securities, including its STRC product, and using the proceeds to acquire Bitcoin. The company then pays dividends to investors while retaining exposure to potential appreciation in its Bitcoin holdings.

Saylor believes the structure could create a self-reinforcing cycle in which additional purchases push Bitcoin prices higher, strengthen Strategy's balance sheet and attract further financing.

Recent findings suggest that “But you can imagine if we sell $40 billion of credit and buy $30 billion of Bitcoin, the price is moving. The price is moving up,” he said.

Higher Bitcoin valuations could subsequently lower perceived credit risk, compress financing spreads and increase demand for Strategy's securities, allowing the organization to raise additional capital.

However, the strategy depends on investors continuing to purchase its credit instruments and the company maintaining sufficient resources to meet dividend obligations.

Saylor acknowledged those constraints elsewhere in his presentation, explaining that Strategy could adjust dividends, deploy dollar reserves, repurchase securities or sell Bitcoin when necessary.

He also said the organization targets roughly 10.5% annual Bitcoin appreciation as the hurdle for capturing excess returns for common shareholders, while estimating that approximately 2% annual appreciation could sustain its dividend commitments under its financial model.

Those projections make the availability and cost of financing key variables in Strategy's planned expansion.

Beyond Strategy's financing model, Saylor expects commercial banks to provide another source of Bitcoin demand by extending credit against investors' existing holdings.

He compared the opportunity to the mortgage market, where access to financing allows buyers to purchase properties without paying their full value upfront.

Saylor specifically identified BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as a potential beneficiary of broader lending arrangements involving JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley and Charles Schwab.

“If Bitcoin flows into an ETF IBIT and if your bank JP Morgan or Morgan Stanley or Schwab will extend credit against the IBIT, you will tend to want to hold that asset. And of course, the better the credit terms they offer, the less incentive you have to sell, the more likely you are to buy.”.

According to recent reports, the arrangement could reduce selling pressure by allowing investors to access cash without liquidating their Bitcoin ETF positions. Lending products that permit investment purchases could also support additional demand.

According to recent reports, saylor pointed to Strategy's proprietary banking adoption index, which he mentioned had increased from 9% approximately three years ago to 34%. The index measures institutional activity across trading, custody, research, derivatives and lending, rather than the volume of Bitcoin-backed credit alone.

However, Charles Schwab's existing Pledged Asset Line illustrates why borrowing against investments does not necessarily guarantee long-term holding power.

The facility allows qualifying investors to borrow against eligible securities without selling them, but its contractual terms give the bank considerable control over repayment.

Schwab can demand repayment at any time, increase collateral requirements without advance written notice and liquidate pledged securities when borrowers fail to satisfy their obligations.

Schwab’s Pledged Asset Line can fund permitted spending without a sale, while the bank keeps the right to demand repayment.

Consider a hypothetical investor borrowing $300,000 against $1 million in securities. A 40% decline in collateral value would increase the loan-to-value ratio from 30% to 50%. If the lender permitted borrowing up to 40% of collateral value, the investor would need to repay $60,000 or provide additional acceptable collateral.

Schwab further prohibits borrowers from using Pledged Asset Line proceeds to purchase securities or spot cryptocurrencies, meaning the product can help preserve existing investments but cannot directly finance additional Bitcoin purchases.

The bank has not established through these disclosures that IBIT qualifies for a particular collateral loan value.

  • Sources indicate that as per CoreX Hosting, about 64,000 Bitcoin miners with a hash rate of 13 EH/s were compromised, and the power was redirected to the OCEAN mining pool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On the 15th of November, Luxor Technology confirmed that its Bitcoin [BTC] mining power was hijacked via Commander software, exposing vulnerabilities in its infrastructure.

Sources indicate that as per CoreX Hosting, about 64,000 Bitcoin miners with a hash rate of 13 EH/s were compromised, and the power was redirected to the OCEAN mining pool. The payouts for miners were allocated to the attacker’s Bitcoin address without authorization.

The X page thought the attack was done by a similar group that compromised Hiveon a couple of days ago. Customers discovered their pool information changed without their knowledge.

Luxor was also compromised in the management software, drawing similarities in the two attacks. Luxor confirmed this activity by writing,.

Affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window.

As a result, the attacked hash rate dropped to 100 PH/s, while that of OCEAN spiked to 48.8 EH/s before falling back to around 40 EH/s.

Sources indicate that the attacker failed to mine a BTC block; hence, they did not receive any reward. However, the attacked miners lost the opportunity to earn rewards, as the hashing time cannot be recovered.

Industry observers note that notably, the frightening aspect was that there was nothing wrong with the miners themselves. The management program perched above them was the weak point.

After realizing the compromise, Luxor Technology’s on-call engineering team jumped into the matter immediately.

It has been revealed that the vulnerability in the Commander software was patched in two hours. However, some say that was the emergency patch, and the extensive restoration took six hours.

Industry observers note that while there was no data leaked from their system, over a dozen clients were affected. The firm promised compensation, saying,.

Every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if it had mined normally.

The tech giant has assured consumers that Commander is operating normally and no action is needed. They also confirmed that Luxor Pool and LuxOS were not impacted.

Sources indicate that with operations now restored and a lined-up compensation, Luxor may restore confidence in users. Some users said the response was not bad at all.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the last Bitcoin is expected to be mined around 2140; thereafter, miners won’t earn upcoming BTC, only transaction fees. That means demand for Bitcoin miners remains high, but security is a concern. Therefore, stronger safeguards are needed to fully restore people’ confidence.

Home » Blitz news » KuCoin Launches 1.1 Million USDT Black Friday Reward Campaign.

Futures traders claim half the rewards, alongside spot, mining, payment cashback, and Tomorrowland Winter perks.

Cryptocurrency exchange KuCoin has rolled out its largest Black Friday promotional event to date, putting more than 1.1 million USDT in rewards on the table as exchanges compete for retail trading volume ahead of the holiday season.

Running from November 16 to December 1, the campaign triples the size of KuCoin’s previous November promotions, which historically ranged from 15,000 USDT to 360,000 USDT.

Unlike past years that focused on single-product giveaways, the 2026 edition spans five trading and payment verticals—and adds VIP hospitality packages for the Tomorrowland Winter 2027 music festival.

The event marks the opening stage of KuCoin’s two-part PROOF series, titled ‘Tis The Season, with a separate Holiday Edition scheduled to follow from December 11 to December 30.

Futures traders stand to receive the largest share of the rewards, with up to 550,000 USDT available through trading-volume competitions, TraderPro return-on-investment (ROI) contests and a lucky draw.

The remaining rewards are spread across other KuCoin services. Spot and margin traders can each compete for up to 100,000 USDT by completing trading tasks and reaching volume targets. VIP owners have up to 150,000 USDT available through trading challenges and volume-based leaderboards, while KuMining is offering up to 100,000 USDT to users who purchase cloud mining hashrate.

Another 100,000 USDT is allocated to crypto payments, with customers able to receive fee cashback when buying or selling cryptocurrencies through bank cards or peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions.

Beyond the trading and payment rewards, the campaign also features a Grand Lucky Draw with additional prizes, including USDT, KuCoin merchandise gift boxes and a Tomorrowland Winter 2027 festival package with accommodation.

The Tomorrowland prizes are part of KuCoin’s partnership with the festival brand. Under the agreement, which runs from 2026 to 2028, KuCoin serves as the Exclusive Crypto Exchange and Crypto Payments Partner for Tomorrowland Winter and Tomorrowland Belgium.

In a recent development, the advertised 1.1 million USDT in prizes covers several types of rewards, rather than direct cash payouts alone. These include fee cashback, trading-related rewards and prizes tied to competition results and trading volumes.

KuCoin has not yet provided details of the second phase, the Holiday Edition, scheduled to run from December 11 to 30. The exchange remarked information about its activities and rewards would be declared separately.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

WhiteBIT has relaunched its over-the-counter (OTC) platform and enhanced its institutional offering with a large-volume trading section for digital assets and fiat currencies. It is tailored for institutional and corporate clients, investment funds, family offices, and other participants in the market that seek a special approach when having high-value deals.

Unlike normal exchange trading, where big orders may impact market prices and execution expenses, OTC trades are transactions carried out outside the public order book, straight between a client and the trading desk. This can reduce the impact on the market, give more flexibility in terms of the execution period, and give more customization for institutional trading.

“The institutional engagement with cryptocurrencies is growing at the level of more than just access to cryptocurrencies. Equipped with a reliable compliance framework, a dedicated team of support, and processes that are predictable in their operations, funds, corporate treasuries, and professional investors require execution models that allow them to operate in the same way they do in traditional financial markets. By relaunching our OTC desk, we’re strengthening the infrastructure that enables these participants to execute large transactions more efficiently and with greater flexibility,” said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group, of which WhiteBIT is a part.

Recent findings suggest that the relaunched desk supports crypto-to-fiat and fiat-to-crypto transactions in major fiat currencies, including the US dollar (USD), euro (EUR), British pound (GBP), and Swiss franc (CHF), as well as the stablecoins USDT and USDC. Also, the top 10 crypto assets by market capitalization are now available for trading on the OTC desk against USDT and USDC. Other crypto assets outside the top 10 and additional fiat currencies are available upon individual request.

Recent findings suggest that whiteBIT does not impose a fixed upper limit on OTC transaction sizes. Instead, the maximum amount is determined by the source of funds and the results of the required compliance checks, so capacity is set around each client’s actual activity.

Each client is assigned to a dedicated OTC manager, who provides them with support in negotiating the transaction parameters, agreeing the terms of execution, and support throughout the transaction. The service protects client data and transactional information and follows Know Your Customer (KYC), Know Your Business (KYB), and all applicable compliance regulations.

Zero Fee Campaign for New OTC Clients.

It has been revealed that whiteBIT is introducing a zero-fee offer for fresh OTC clients, covering their first transaction of up to $2 million. It is a one-time offer, valid for three months from release, after which it can be extended; transactions with the top 10 crypto assets are not covered by the offer. Deals with a value of more than 2 million are processed as a single tranche with an indicative price derived from the OTC pricing strategy established in advance with the client’s dedicated OTC manager, allowing institutional and corporate clients to plan bigger deals from the beginning.

The relaunch is a part of WhiteBIT’s institutional and professional market business growth strategy. With the addition of a dedicated OTC execution channel, WhiteBIT will aim to provide crypto liquidity and allow more flexibility in handling large-scale digital asset transactions for businesses and investors.

It has been revealed that whiteBIT is a leading global crypto exchange by user traffic, offering over 1020 trading pairs, 370+ assets, and supporting 8 fiat currencies. With a strong focus on regulatory compliance, WhiteBIT serves 10 million users across six continents and more than 150 countries. Founded in 2018, the platform is part of W Group, which has more than 40 million customers globally. WhiteBIT collaborates with Visa, FACEIT, FC Barcelona, Juventus FC, and the Ukrainian national football team. The organization is dedicated to driving the widespread adoption of blockchain technology worldwide.

Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab declared new tools for quantum error correction on Nov. 16, and the news comes amid a debate in the crypto industry about "Q-Day," the moment when a quantum computer will be able to break Bitcoin's cryptography. As of Monday, the price of Bitcoin stands at $64,580.

It has been revealed that nvidia released a new decoding algorithm, TCBP-JOBS, on Nov. 16. According to the tech giant, the algorithm delivers up to 13,000x faster decoding compared with existing leading algorithms, and it cuts the computation time for researching new quantum computing designs from 12 weeks to 45 minutes.

Nvidia remarked that the algorithm helps researchers find designs that use physical qubits more efficiently, "shortening the path to practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.".

Nvidia and IBM also revealed plans for a modular quantum computing codesign platform with Fermilab. IBM and Nvidia are placing Nvidia DGX B200 systems next to IBM quantum computers, including those powered by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, and researchers will use the platform to develop and test error-correction codes.

"Making quantum computers useful for science requires advances in error correction, applications and the systems that bring quantum processors and accelerated computing together," said Krysta Svore, vice president of applied research for quantum computing at Nvidia.

A 2022 study by researchers from the University of Sussex estimated that breaking Bitcoin's encryption within a day would require around 13 million physical qubits.

It has been revealed that IBM Quantum Nighthawk, which IBM calls its fastest quantum processor, has 120 qubits. According to Nvidia, errors in quantum processors "limit the complexity and duration of the computations they can perform.".

Sources indicate that in 2024, Bitcoin developer Hunter Beast proposed BIP-360, a fresh output type that would protect coins from quantum attacks. In July 2025, Casa co-founder Jameson Lopp also suggested a blueprint to phase out legacy signatures and move coins to quantum-resistant addresses.

Early coins mined by Satoshi Nakamoto sit on addresses with public keys that are already visible on the blockchain.

In November 2024, NIST proposed to stop allowing vulnerable public-key algorithms, including elliptic curve cryptography, after 2035.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leading cryptocurrency Bitcoin has dropped 5.6% on the day, and is currently trading at just over $69,300, per Decrypt data. It comes after the latest consumer price index, or CPI, results came in "hotter than expected," experts noted, with the drop was triggered by a "concentrated liquidation.".

Bitcoin's plunge took it to a 24-hour low of $67,922, its lowest level since mid-August, when it boosted from $63,000.

"Bitcoin’s drop below $69,000 was directly triggered by a concentrated liquidation of leveraged long positions," Tim Sun, senior analyst at Hashkey, told Decrypt. "Though the deeper concern lies in steadily weakening market demand.".

Sun highlighted U.S. Bitcoin spot ETFs recording six consecutive days of net outflows, according to CoinGlass. He also pointed to stablecoin supply shrinking and MSCI removing digital asset treasury firm Strategy from its funds.

"ETFs, stablecoin liquidity, and corporate treasuries have served as the primary capital pillars supporting this Bitcoin rally," Sun remarked. "With all three coming under simultaneous pressure, the market is losing the marginal buying power that previously propelled prices higher.".

It has been revealed that meanwhile, other major cryptocurrencies have also taken a hit. Ethereum has dropped 4.6% on the day to $1,953, BNB has slipped 4.7% to $639.46, and Solana is down 3.1% to $80.47, according to Decrypt data. The global crypto market cap has dropped 4.6% over the past 24 hours to $2.39 trillion.

Industry observers note that it follows U.S. CPI rising 0.4% in October, which is "hotter than expected, even if the headline monthly rate eased to 0.4% from September’s 0.6%," according to CoinShares head of research James Butterfill. "More troubling was the composition," he added. "Food rose 0.5%, services remained firm, and core CPI increased 0.3%, with services excluding rent, a gauge of domestic price pressure the Fed watches closely, rising 0.5%. The inflation problem is therefore no longer easily dismissed as an oil story.".

Sources indicate that the consumer price index, or CPI, is a way of measuring inflation that tracks the average price changes of everyday goods and services over time. Central banks tend to use CPI to inform whether they'll cut or hike interest rates, meaning higher-than-expected CPI signals a potential Federal Reserve hike.

In a recent development, polymarket predictors put a 97% chance on the Fed raising interest rates this year, up from 75% at the start of the week. The CME FedWatch tool, meanwhile, sees an 88% chance of a 25 basis point hike, with 12% anticipating a 50 basis point rise.

On top of the CPI, Bitcoin's downward move comes following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the tech giant, after reports of multiple affairs including with a suspected Chinese spy and a senior company executive spread.

In a recent development, huang's departure has sparked "severe volatility across tech stocks, further dampening market risk appetite," Sun told Decrypt. "This has prompted broader portfolio de-risking, amplifying the downward pressure on Bitcoin," he added.

For a crypto rebound to happen, Sun noted that Bitcoin needs "long-term allocation capital" to flow back into crypto after ETFs, stablecoins, and digital asset treasury companies have taken a hit in recent weeks.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kava plans to retire HARD Lend's borrowing functionality after hackers stole 53.9 million KAVA, leaving the lending protocol facing a substantial liquidity shortfall.
  • The blockchain network confirmed on Nov.
  • The stolen tokens were worth $3.7 million before the subsequent market selloff, according to blockchain analytics firm Bitquery.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kava plans to retire HARD Lend's borrowing functionality after hackers stole 53.9 million KAVA, leaving the lending protocol facing a substantial liquidity shortfall.

The blockchain network confirmed on Nov. 16 that the Nov. 14 attack exploited a vulnerability in HARD Lend's accounting system, allowing attackers to withdraw existing KAVA tokens through manipulated collateral and liquidation transactions.

The stolen tokens were worth $3.7 million before the subsequent market selloff, according to blockchain analytics firm Bitquery.

Kava said it had patched the vulnerability and introduced safeguards to prevent attackers from repeating the exploit. It also accelerated looks to retire the lending service, with a governance proposal expected to permanently disable new lending and borrowing.

The proposal must pass a seven-day governance voting process, while existing protective measures remain in force.

“The planned retirement of HARD Lend's legacy lending functionality is being accelerated,” Kava said, adding that it would address remaining positions through an orderly process.

The manufacturer emphasized that the breach was confined to HARD Lend and did not compromise the underlying Kava blockchain or create additional tokens.

However, the incident has raised questions about how the protocol will settle outstanding obligations after losing almost all the tokens available in its lending pool.

Kava noted attackers manipulated the value of BUSD collateral within HARD Lend, allowing them to repeatedly borrow KAVA and trigger liquidations that cleared their debts without recovering the borrowed tokens.

An investigation by blockchain analysis firm Bitquery found that the attackers borrowed about 55.2 million KAVA across 127 transactions and retained 53.9 million tokens after repayments involving other borrowers.

The attackers subsequently moved about 49.2 million KAVA to BNB Chain through LayerZero.

Bitquery traced the sale of 48.4 million KAVA, which generated approximately $2.09 million in BNB and USDT.

The investigation also identified a failed transaction involving 612,416 USDT through the Relay bridge. The service rejected the transfer with a “BLOCKED_WALLET” message, preventing the requested payout to Ethereum.

November 14 evidence describes three distinct access paths: lender claims, a failed bridge order and exchange transfers.

Lender withdrawals require usable KAVA in the pool. Blocking a bridge payout or reopening exchange transfers does not itself supply that cash.

Pool and bridge observations are dated November 14. Relay record was read at 16:20 UTC; BNB Chain/Ethereum data end at 16:08 UTC. The withdrawable flag was untested. Coinone notice is not a live status feed.

According to recent reports, select dated reported balances and access states. Connectors depict access routes only, not quantitative flows. Pool outline is schematic, not proportional. No derived totals, valuations or exchange conversions.

Industry observers note that pool and bridge observations are dated November 14. Relay record was read at 16:20 UTC; BNB Chain/Ethereum data end at 16:08 UTC. The withdrawable flag was untested. Coinone notice is not a live status feed.

Kava separately confirmed that part of the attackers' funds had been frozen and noted it was working with exchanges, ecosystem partners, and law enforcement to trace and recover the remaining assets.

However, it did not disclose how much had been secured or whether the frozen funds included the USDT identified by Bitquery.

The recovery efforts have yet to resolve the more immediate problem facing HARD Lend's depositors.

Bitquery's Nov. 14 reconstruction showed that the lending pool owed owners approximately 55.2 million KAVA while holding just 0.19 KAVA available for withdrawals.

The blockchain network mentioned “Individual user deposits were largely unaffected,” but did not explain how that assessment relates to outstanding lender claims or depleted pool liquidity. It also promised further guidance for affected owners as the retirement proposal progresses.

It has been revealed that for all of the havoc dementia causes to a person's life, scientists are still trying to figure out exactly how to prevent it. While keeping your brain and body active and following a healthy diet seems to help, there doesn't seem to be a pill you can pop to lower your risk of developing the devastating disease. But new research suggests that a common osteoporosis drug might be worth investigating further.

It's a class of medications called nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates (or NBPs). While these are typically used to strengthen bones in people with osteoporosis, NBPs could have the added benefit of supporting brain health as you age, too.

According to recent reports, it's key to stress this now: The researchers found a link between people who used NBPs and a lower risk of dementia, but they didn't prove that the medications themselves actually dropped the risk. Still, doctors say there could be something to this. "The association is intriguing," says Anna Hohler, MD, director of neurology for Northwell Health's Westchester Region, and chair of neurology at Phelps Hospital and Northern Westchester Hospital.

Here's what experts want you to take away from the findings.

Meet the experts: Ching-Lung Cheung, PhD, study co-author and associate professor in the Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacy at the University of Hong Kong; Clifford Segil, DO, a neurologist at Providence Saint John's Health Center in Santa Monica, California; and Anna Hohler, MD, director of neurology for Northwell Health's Westchester Region, and chair of neurology at Phelps Hospital and Northern Westchester Hospital.

In a recent development, the study, which was published in the journal Alzheimer's & Dementia, analyzed the electronic medical records of more than 120,000 patients aged 60 and older in Hong Kong. All of the participants had osteoporosis or fractures due to fragility (meaning, their bones had weakened).

Sources indicate that researchers discovered that people who took NBPs had a 16 percent lower risk of developing Alzheimer's disease and related dementias compared to those who didn't take medication for osteoporosis. But when they compared those who used NBPs to those taking other types of osteoporosis medications, the dementia risk was 24 percent lower.

The link seemed to be especially strong in women and patients who had hip fractures.

In a recent development, the researchers were inspired to look into NBPs and Alzheimer’s because the drug had been shown to improve cognitive function in previous animal models of neurotoxicity and Alzheimer’s disease, notes Ching-Lung Cheung, PhD, study co-author and associate professor in the Department of Pharmacology and Pharmacy at the University of Hong Kong. “These findings led us to investigate whether their use might also be associated with a lower risk of dementia in humans.".

While the study didn't prove that NBPs were responsible for the lowered risk, doctors have a few theories on what could be driving this.

For one, it’s possible that the link is more indirect, according to Clifford Segil, DO, a neurologist at Providence Saint John's Health Center in Santa Monica, California. NBPs improve bone density over time, which allows people to be more active, Dr. Segil indicates. "Broken bones do not cause dementia but do decrease activity," he says. (Being sedentary is a risk factor for dementia.).

Industry observers note that there may also be something about NBPs themselves that could lower the risk of dementia, though. "Some researchers speculate that these medications could influence inflammation, immune pathways, or other biological processes involved in neurodegeneration," Dr. Hoehler claims. But, she points out, more research is needed.

In a recent development, for now, doctors don't initiative to prescribe NBPs in an effort to lower dementia risk. But Dr. Cheung says it should make people feel confident about using this class of medication for bone health. "Given the low uptake of osteoporosis treatment, people with osteoporosis should consider appropriate anti-osteoporosis medication, which may offer an additional benefit for brain health," he says. Even though osteoporosis drugs are commonly available, uptake has been historically low—studies have previously estimated that around seven percent of women with osteoporosis actually take medication for it.

Ultimately, doctors say that a clinical trial is needed to see if NBPs actually lower the risk of dementia. "If future studies confirm these results, they could open an exciting fresh avenue for Alzheimer's prevention or treatment," Dr. Hoehler claims.

It has been revealed that carina Hsieh, MPH, is the deputy features editor of Women’s Health. She has more than a decade’s worth of experience working in media and has covered everything from beauty, fashion, travel, lifestyle, pets, to health.

She began her career as an intern in the fashion closet at Cosmopolitan where she worked her way up to Senior Sex & Relationships Editor. While covering women’s health there, she discovered her passion for health service journalism and took a break to get her Masters in Public Health. Post-grad school, she worked as a freelance writer and as The Daily Beast’s first Beauty, Health, and Wellness Reporter.

In a recent development, carina is an alum of the Fashion Institute of Technology and the Yale School of Public Health. She and her French Bulldog, Bao Bao, split their time between Brooklyn and Connecticut. She enjoys reformer Pilates, (slow) running, and smelling the fancy toiletries in boutique fitness class locker rooms.

Elite university Harvard maintains significant Bitcoin exposure as it holds over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin ETF, a recent regulatory filing has revealed.

Harvard University remains highly exposed to Bitcoin (BTC) as the elite institution continues to hold over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF).

In a recent development, as per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Company, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

The Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) showed that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

According to recent reports, as per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

Industry observers note that for instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

According to recent reports, later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

Sources indicate that during the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

Since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Harvard University is not the only top-tier American university that has gained exposure to the biggest cryptocurrency by market capitalization.

Sources indicate that in October 2024, Emory University became the first U.S. university endowment to publicly disclose its holdings in a Bitcoin ETF.

It held roughly 2.7 million shares of Grayscale’s Bitcoin Mini Trust, worth over $15 million at the time.

Meanwhile, in May 2025, Brown University disclosed its holdings of 105,000 shares of BlackRock's IBIT, worth roughly $4.9 million as of March 31 of that year.

Later, Brown doubled its stake, bringing its holdings to 212,500 shares.

Meanwhile, Dartmouth College has also joined the list of universities with exposure to cryptocurrency ETFs.

In its recent filing, Dartmouth College disclosed that it held 201,531 IBIT shares. The investment was worth roughly $9.5 million as of the end of September 2026.

The demand in question came from an open letter urging Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse to burn the full remaining escrow, presently about 31.1 billion XRP, by the first quarter of 2027. At recent prices near $0.95, that amount is worth roughly $30 billion.

Ripple locked 55 billion XRP into on-ledger escrow contracts in December, 2017 specifically to make supply more predictable.

Each month, up to 1 billion XRP becomes available; historically, the company has re-locked the majority into newly introduced smart contracts further down the line and retained a smaller net amount for operational use.

In a recent development, it would make more sense for XRPL validators to vote on any major supply change, because the XRP Ledger is decentralized. Ripple runs only a small share of the default Unique Node List (roughly 1 of ~35, or low single-digit percent).Protocol amendments require ~80% of trusted… https://t.co/Ib7cTsQHUx.

The escrow balance has already declined from 55 billion to roughly 31.1 billion as a result of this process.

Destroying the remaining escrow would mean permanently removing an asset that sits on Ripple’s balance sheet and that the manufacturer has repeatedly said is intended for controlled distribution, partnerships, and ecosystem growth.

No public firm has ever willingly incinerated tens of billions of dollars in assets simply because a segment of token holders asked for it.

It has been revealed that morgan has addressed similar proposals before. He has pointed out that large burns by other projects, including Stellar’s well-known reduction of its XLM supply, did not produce lasting price strength or prevent later declines.

The recurring demand to burn the XRP escrow, in his view, often functions more as a signal that the requester doubts the asset’s underlying value than as a coherent supply-side strategy.

Critics of the XRP escrow schedule frequently treat every monthly unlock as an automatic dump that suppresses price.

In practice, the majority of each release is returned to escrow, and XRP’s price has continued to move largely in line with broader crypto market conditions rather than in lockstep with the XRP escrow schedule.

The supply was never meant to last forever. At the current net release rate of roughly 300 million XRP per month, the locked supply continues to decline gradually.

Imagine asking a tech giant to destroy an asset valued at $30 billion, believe they would ever do it, and expect to be viewed as sane https://t.co/sft8TRMV80.

Morgan the lawyer has also noted in earlier posts that the escrow has already fallen from 55 billion in late 2017 to the low-to-mid 30s of billions today.

Hardware wallet maker Trezor has slashed its reseller network by about 80% after discovering malicious implants that can steal cryptocurrency recovery phrases from devices sold through a third-party distributor.

It has been revealed that the company confirmed on Nov. 12 that three Trezor Safe 5 wallets purchased from Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis contained hidden electronic components designed to capture sensitive information and transmit it to attackers.

Trezor also released firmware version 2.13.1 on Nov. 11 to disable the identified implants, although it warned that customers whose recovery phrases may have been exposed must still transfer their assets to newly created wallets.

The findings follow an October supply-chain security incident involving CryptoBilis and Ledger hardware wallets, which investigators linked to cryptocurrency thefts exceeding $86 million.

It has been revealed that blockchain analytics firm Bitquery subsequently traced approximately $102 million in losses across 335 wallets on six blockchains. Ledger confirmed finding a malicious hardware implant in a customer's device, although investigators have not established that the implant caused every reported loss.

The incidents exposed vulnerabilities in hardware-wallet distribution, where attackers can modify genuine devices before customers receive them.

In a recent development, trezor identified three compromised Safe 5 devices purchased between Aug. 20 and Sept. 23 through CryptoBilis's Tokopedia and Shopee storefronts and direct sales.

Its security team physically examined one device and identified the other two through photographs supplied by their owners.

The attackers installed an additional circuit board between the wallet's main board and display, allowing the implant to monitor information shown on the screen without modifying the firmware or Secure Element.

Trezor’s defense stops the implants it identified from capturing more data. A backup captured earlier creates a separate recovery problem.

Industry observers note that trezor notes 2.13.1 blocks the identified implants on devices running it. An earlier seed copy remains a separate risk.

Trezor tells affected buyers to create a wallet with a new seed and move funds. Loading the old backup onto new hardware does not solve exposure.

In a recent development, trezor is tightening device sourcing, storage and access. These controls address the path to the buyer, before any secret is exposed.

For buyers covered by Trezor’s warning, moving funds to a new wallet with a fresh seed addresses possible earlier capture.

According to recent reports, trezor’s firmware assurance applies to identified implants. Diagrams do not establish that every buyer’s seed was captured, prove losses, or show completed customer migration. A newly introduced seed must accompany movement of funds.

It has been revealed that qualitative map of Trezor’s reported display interception and recovery guidance. Dashed paths show possible prior capture, not observed theft. Selectable diagrams compare intervention points; no geometry represents quantities or prevalence.

Trezor’s firmware assurance applies to identified implants. Diagrams do not establish that every buyer’s seed was captured, prove losses, or show completed customer migration. A new seed must accompany movement of funds.

The component could capture recovery phrases during wallet setup or restoration, along with passphrases displayed on the device.

Industry observers note that it then encrypted the information and transmitted it through a mobile network to an attacker-controlled server. When connectivity was unavailable, the implant stored the data and retried transmission.

It has been revealed that the attack exploited a critical weakness in cryptocurrency self-custody. Anyone who obtains a wallet's recovery phrase can potentially restore control over its assets without possessing the original hardware.

Trezor said its latest firmware prevents the identified implants from collecting additional information, but it cannot invalidate recovery credentials attackers may already possess.

Consequently, the manufacturer has urged anyone who purchased a Trezor from CryptoBilis since March 2026 to create a new wallet with a different recovery phrase and move their funds.

The tech giant has offered eligible customers replacement devices or refunds.

Trezor said 48 CryptoBilis customers had contacted it during the investigation. None of the three confirmed implant owners reported losing funds, and investigators found no evidence of similar tampering in devices examined from other resellers.

Meanwhile, Trezor is tightening requirements governing how its remaining distributors source, store, and handle devices.

The company continues working with cryptocurrency security response group SEAL 911 to investigate the compromises.

The unresolved risk concerns recovery phrases captured before the firmware upgrade. Customers whose credentials were exposed remain vulnerable until they move their cryptocurrency to wallets secured by entirely new recovery credentials.

Only the rack is labeled with weight numbers, not the actual dumbbell."I think this is an ideal product for someone who knows their way around a gym and is looking for a solid addition to their home to supplement," indicates Howell. "They're perfect for an intermediate client.".

According to recent reports, in terms of sound, while "these are quieter than other adjustable dumbbells on the market, they make more noise than the PowerBlocks," explains Samuel. Additionally, if you wish to incorporate barbell movements into your home workout routine, we've found that these dumbbells work seamlessly with the Hyperbell.

One of my favorite equipment makers, I was surprised how long it took REP Fitness to come out with a viable adjustable dumbbell option. But it seems like they were waiting to create something special, and that's what they've done with the QuickDraws.

In a recent development, the plates can be adjusted in 2.5-pound increments, spanning from 5 to 30 pounds. For those heavy lifters, 30 pounds might not be enough, but for the average user looking for a quick pump in the arms or lighter weights for perfect accessory movements, this is a great pick. For anyone who wants to increase the weight, REP Fitness offers heavier options with the same streamlined design, for up to 60 pounds.

They've patented their Lock-N-Load adjustment system, which is straightforward and lets you change the weights by flipping a switch on each dumbbell. This system allows you to swap weights quickly, so you can change the load between dumbbell exercises and avoid stalling.

For our testing, the dumbbells arrived in two boxes and require minimal assembly, making them an ultra-accessible choice for delivery and home use.

PowerBlock adjustable dumbbells are an ultra-sturdy set designed for lasting performance, perfect for executing heavy-duty moves like dead stop rows, Romanian deadlifts, and heavy presses. At just 12 inches long with the storage stand, these dumbbells offer decent compactness and versatility.

It has been revealed that the Pro 50 Adjustable Dumbbells cover a weight range of 5 to 50 pounds per dumbbell, with adjustments in increments of 2.5 pounds. This weight range suits beginners well, and more experienced lifters can expand the weight by opting for additional expansion kits. For those who find 50 pounds per dumbbell insufficient, PowerBlock offers heavier models such as the Elite USA (up to 90 pounds per dumbbell) or the Pro 100 EXP (up to 100 pounds per dumbbell). Most models of adjustable dumbbells by PowerBlock feature the same pin-and-lock adjustment mechanism, which is easy to use and avoids jamming concerns found in some other systems.

Industry observers note that in his testing, Howell pointed out the compact structure of the actual dumbbell, noting the plate-like weights, which are more like weighted frames than traditional circular ones. Howell found this design "genius", as the square nature of the dumbbell makes it easy to lay down once done using it without it rolling away or requiring a rack to rest it in. He also appreciated that they arrived assembled and were fairly easy to unpack and begin using.

However, Howell expressed concerns about the durability of certain components, such as the handles and the "clip" that allows you to lock your chosen weight in, which are made of plastic. He believes these dumbbells might not be robust enough for consistent use, particularly for hardcore gymgoers.

Despite these concerns, Samuel praises their adjustability and durability, stating, "I've never encountered a more durable adjustable dumbbell. I love them for farmer’s walks, heavy DB lunges, and thrusters, and rely on them anytime I do a metcon-style workout at home." Samuel also shared he’s dropped these from three or four feet up after tough sets of incline presses, "and they hold up just fine." (Although it's not advisable to make a habit of dropping any adjustable dumbbells regularly.)These dumbbells feature comfortable contoured handles that enhance grip during workouts. However, they do not provide the same weight distribution as traditional dumbbells, as Samuel points out: "If you’re looking to use a set of adjustable movements for plenty of accessory movements, go with something more dumbbell-shaped.".

Look for a weight range that meets your fitness goals. Most adjustable dumbbells can be adjusted in 2.5- or 5-pound increments, so it's key to consider a weight range that fits your needs.

According to recent reports, adjustable dumbbells come in different shapes and sizes. Consider the size and shape of the dumbbells and make sure they feel comfortable in your hands. Basically, does the dumbbell feel "good" or natural to you? Again, this comes down to personal preference and might involve some trial and error.

Recent findings suggest that some adjustable dumbbells distribute the load differently than traditional dumbbells (atypical), changing how it responds to certain movements (particularly accessory movements). A good rule of thumb is if you're looking to perform heavier exercises (farmer's carries, RDLs, rows) you can consider an adjustable dumbbell that doesn't distribute its weight like a traditional dumbbell, such as the PowerBlock option featured above. If you're planning to do more accessory movements (like biceps curls or skull crushers), opt for a traditional dumbbell-shaped option.

There are a few different mechanisms adjustable dumbbells use to switch weights, with some being easier or more user-friendly.

This mechanism uses a dial on the end of the dumbbell handle to adjust the weight. To change the weight, you turn the dial to the desired weight, and the mechanism will lock in the appropriate weight plates. Some adjustable dumbbells must be docked in their storage base to change weight using a dial, while others can be adjusted outside their docking station.

This mechanism uses a pin to select the desired weight and can take some practice to get used to if you're new to it. To change the weight, pull out the pin, select the desired weight, then reinsert the pin into the corresponding slot to lock it in.

Sources indicate that this mechanism uses a twist-locking mechanism to secure the weight plates. To change the weight, you twist the handle to unlock the weight plates, remove or add weight plates, and then twist the handle back to lock in the upcoming weight.

Warranties reflect a manufacturer's confidence in its product. And with some of the best adjustable dumbbells priced at or above $500, you want to be sure your investment is protected. So, it’s vital to purchase from a manufacturer that offers a clear, comprehensive warranty. They vary widely across the industry, with the most budget-forward brands offering just 90 days on some parts, and others boasting generous five-year warranties on everything. Again, the more you spend upfront, the better the warranty is likely to be. And, if there’s anything that isn’t clear to you about the stated warranty, be sure to ask. It’s your money, after all.

Industry observers note that as the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men's Health, it's my job to test the latest and greatest training equipment, including adjustable dumbbells. To build this guide, I tested more than 30 adjustable dumbbells over the past five years, drawing on my experience and that of my fellow MH fitness editors, including Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., and Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM. Samuel utilized the top-performing adjustable dumbbells featured in this guide in fitness programs with several of his advanced clients.

Sources indicate that we also enlisted the help of Maillard Howell of Dean CrossFit in Brooklyn, to test and assess how well these dumbbells performed in the real world (read: a high-traffic training facility). In addition, we sought insights from trainers from both our MH Advisory Board and our Strength in Diversity class for further anecdotal and experiential perspectives on the top adjustable dumbbells.

Each dumbbell was rigorously tested in a variety of categories, including durability, weight distribution, ease of shifting between weights, and aesthetics. All dumbbells were tested with three types of exercises: explosive exercises (such as cleans), multi-joint strength exercises (such as bench presses and Romanian deadlifts), and accessory movements (such as biceps curls and lateral raises). All dumbbells were also dropped from a standard bench to test baseline durability (no adjustable dumbbell should ever be dropped from shoulder height), and they were monitored for signs of rust over a three-month period.

Adjustable dumbbells pack a ton of perks compared to regular dumbbells, with the most obvious being their space-saving design: No matter which adjustable dumbbells you choose, you can guarantee they'll take up less space than the sets of traditional dumbbells they replace.

Another attractive benefit of adjustable dumbbells is that they're more cost-effective than multiple sets of traditional dumbbells. A lot of the options on this list aren't exactly budget buys, we know. But building out a weight rack with 5-15 sets of high-quality traditional dumbbells can add up in cost even quicker.

This comes down to three things: space, personal preference, and how you blueprint to use your dumbbells. If you have unlimited space, you can definitely consider standard dumbbells.

"If you're building out a home gym and especially if you like to train accessory motions and work through a full range of motion, you still can't beat standard dumbbells," explains Samuel.

"They're going to be more durable, have better weight distribution for most moves, and, as cool as some adjustment dial might be, there's nothing more efficient than literally putting a 35-pound dumbbell down and picking a 40-pounder up.".

According to recent reports, but if you're in tight confines or like to work out on the go, opt for a good adjustable option. "You can load a pair of Powerblocks in your trunk much more easily than you can load 10 pairs of dumbbells for a road trip.".

Industry observers note that you'll also want to consider how often you'll drop your dumbbells. Even the best, most durable adjustable dumbbells on this list still have weight-switching mechanisms and won't hold up to being routinely dropped from a few feet in the air after a set of shoulder presses as well as standard dumbbells.

It has been revealed that the weight of adjustable dumbbells depends on your fitness level and goals. Typically, they come in two main categories: those that max out at around 50 pounds per dumbbell and those that start at 50 pounds and get way heavier.

For beginners and folks looking to engage in moderate strength training at home, a set that maxes out at 50 pounds per dumbbell should suffice. They offer a range of weights for a wide variety of exercises and are a great starting point. Beginners can work on everything from biceps curls to overhead presses to squats with these.

Sources indicate that now, if you're a seasoned lifter, powerlifter, or someone aiming to build strength, opt for a pair of adjustable dumbbells that can go well above 50 pounds per bell. Adjustable sets from SMRTFT can offer a max of 80 pounds and 100 pounds per bell, respectively. For experienced lifters, added weight means greater versatility in tackling heavy exercises and challenging yourself.

Just like standard dumbbells, adjustable dumbbells are safe when used correctly and with proper form. But, as with any type of fitness equipment, there are some safety considerations to keep in mind.

Sources indicate that it's important to choose adjustable dumbbells that are well-made and constructed from durable materials. If you're using an old-school model with removable plates, make sure they're securely attached to the handle before you start your lift.

The shape, feel, and weight distribution of adjustable dumbbells can take some getting used to, depending on the model you're working with. Because they may feel different compared to standard dumbbells in movements you do regularly, it's important to focus on slow, controlled movements and proper form throughout your workout (especially as you acclimate to them).

  • In a recent development, in his Nov.
  • The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

In a recent development, in his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz said they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet said that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

Some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating newly introduced ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," mentioned Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a new cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz noted it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

Recent findings suggest that "It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz remarked.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bitcoin‘s recovery above $64,000 risks losing momentum as leveraged traders dominate market activity while institutional investors continue withdrawing capital.

Recent findings suggest that the cryptocurrency staged a modest rebound after plunging toward $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest level since July. However, the recovery comes against a backdrop of weakening demand, with US spot Bitcoin ETFs recording substantial withdrawals and futures positions shrinking across major exchanges.

The clearest warning came from Wall Street before the weekend crash.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw more than $1 billion in net outflows over the five trading sessions ending Nov. 13. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for about $908 million of those withdrawals, highlighting a retreat from one of Bitcoin's largest institutional investment channels.

With ETF demand retreating, leveraged traders dominated the weekend's market activity.

A CryptoQuant analysis showed that Bitcoin futures generated $64.11 billion in trading volume on Nov. 14, dwarfing the $13.36 billion recorded across tracked spot exchanges.

That meant derivatives accounted for nearly 83% of combined trading activity, with futures turnover almost five times larger than spot volume.

The imbalance was particularly striking on Binance, where $24.46 billion in Bitcoin futures trading exceeded the combined spot volume of every exchange tracked by CryptoQuant by 83%.

Recent findings suggest that the disparity raises a troubling possibility for Bitcoin's recovery. Prices may stabilize as leveraged traders unwind bearish positions, but that buying can disappear promptly if investors don't return to accumulate the underlying cryptocurrency.

The weekend's derivatives frenzy coincided with a significant retreat in open interest, suggesting traders were reducing exposure as Bitcoin absorbed its latest losses.

It has been revealed that binance data showed that open interest in its coin-margined Bitcoin futures market dropped 7.3%, from 16.25 million contracts on Nov. 13 to 15.06 million by Monday morning.

The perpetual futures segment contracted even faster, declining approximately 7.8% over the same period.

In a recent development, nov 13–16, 2026: Binance's BTCUSD coin-margined contracts shrank 7.3%. Perpetual funding had returned to positive territory by Monday morning.

It has been revealed that nov 15: −0.006022%. Shorts paid longs at this settlement.

Nov 16: +0.003593%. Longs paid shorts; funding was already positive by Sunday at 16:00 UTC.

Sources indicate that the count establishes a contraction in one Binance segment. Funding demonstrates payment direction; neither proves a lasting Bitcoin recovery.

That reduction removed more than 1.18 million outstanding contracts from Binance's coin-margined market, reducing the pool of speculative positions that had helped fuel the weekend's volatility.

Meanwhile, funding rates revealed another significant shift in trading conditions.

In a recent development, binance's BTCUSD perpetual funding rate turned negative at -0.006022% on Nov. 15 as bearish pressure intensified. By Monday morning, the rate had reversed to 0.003593%, indicating that the earlier imbalance favoring short positions had eased.

Together, falling open interest and the funding reversal suggest Bitcoin's derivatives market has undergone a substantial reset.

They also leave room for a short-covering rebound, in which traders who bet on further losses buy futures contracts to close their positions, potentially pushing prices higher without attracting fresh spot investment.

However, the danger is that such buying is temporary.

Once bearish traders finish closing their positions, that source of demand disappears. Unless fresh buyers step in, Bitcoin could lose the support behind its recovery and become vulnerable to another round of selling.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

It has been revealed that if I’ve learned anything over the past few years, it’s to just say yes. Saying the word was simple, but ended up changing my relationship with fitness—and transforming my whole life.

I’ve always loved being physically active and moving my body; I ran track and field in high school, played field hockey in both high school and college, and enjoyed horseback riding as a young adult. But shortly after graduating, I had my first of seven children at 23. From that point on, I went straight into parenting mode: My family became my priority, and with so much to juggle, exercise took a back seat for the next few decades.

Industry observers note that but at 55, I wanted to feel strong in my body again. My kids were grown and I had more free time, so I signed up for a gym membership. I even started working with a personal trainer to make sure I was doing the right moves safely. Over the next 15 years, I exercised with several trainers, lifting light weights once or twice a week with dumbbells and weight machines. I enjoyed the workouts and saw improvements to my overall fitness, but I wasn’t particularly passionate about going to the gym, so I wasn’t always consistent and never set any real goals.

It has been revealed that then, at 70, everything changed. My trainer who I had come to enjoy working with and trust moved away, and without that connection, I stopped going to the gym. But after about a year away, the fitness manager at my gym, Nate Fleming, reached out to me, and I began working with him twice a week.

According to recent reports, he immediately changed up my programming and introduced me to the idea of progressive overload. I learned that gradually increasing the weight I lifted each week could help me build muscle, get stronger, and see real results. He also added upcoming movements to my routine, like farmer’s carries, deadlifts, and squat variations. Deadlifts, in particular, became one of my favorite exercises—I loved that the move required so much technique. There was something so satisfying about picking up a heavy weight and realizing I could lift more than I thought.

Nearly overnight, my attitude toward fitness changed: I enjoyed being challenged and discovering how much stronger I could become when I pushed myself. Over the next year, I began to see visible muscle definition in my arms and legs and felt more energized throughout the day. More importantly, though, my confidence skyrocketed because I had developed a greater trust in my own abilities.

It has been revealed that I had grown to love lifting heavy, and wanted to step outside my comfort zone and discover what I could accomplish in my 70s. I casually asked Nate if there were deadlifting competitions for older women, and he mentioned there were. So, I took a leap of faith and started a seven-month training process for a powerlifting competition (which took place this past March). I upped my training to three days a week, continuing to progressively increase the weights, and worked on refining my technique to move more efficiently.

It has been revealed that the day of the competition was one of the best days of my life. I decided to compete in all three lifts: I squatted 132 pounds, bench-pressed 71.5 pounds, and deadlifted 242 pounds, setting records in all three lifts for my age and weight category in Nova Scotia, Canada, where I live. I was so proud of what I’d accomplished and felt incredibly empowered by what my body could do at 71. My kids and grandkids were also there to cheer me on, which made the day even more special. Sharing that moment with my family and showing them what was possible at my age meant so much to me. I walked away feeling stronger, more confident, and excited to do it again.

My next powerlifting competition is this month, and I still lift with Nate three days a week. My training is structured in four-week blocks, and the weight, sets, and reps change each week. For instance, in week one, I might do 3 sets of 5 reps at a moderate weight. Then, I gradually increase the load in weeks two and three while lowering the reps as I get closer to my heaviest lifts. Week four is a deload week, so I reduce the weight and give my body a chance to recover before lifting heavier again.

Recent findings suggest that each workout starts with the main lift (deadlift, squat, or bench press) because that’s when I have the most energy. Then, I move on to three or four accessory exercises, where I use lighter weights to strengthen supporting muscles, address weaknesses, and improve my performance in the main lifts. For example, on deadlift day, I might incorporate exercises like lunges, hamstring curls, and bent-over rows to strengthen my glutes, hamstrings, and back.

I’m incredibly proud of my progress over the last six months. I have a lingering shoulder injury, so right now, my bench press has stayed about the same at 71.5 pounds. But I can squat 160 pounds and deadlift 265 pounds, which is only five pounds away from the Canadian deadlift record.

While I train hard, I recover even harder in between sessions. I get seven to eight hours of sleep each night and am mindful about nutrition, eating lots of protein, since it’s important for building and maintaining muscle. I aim for around 120 grams a day, with eggs, chicken, and fish as some of my go-to sources. Additionally, during rest days, I focus on stretching and hip and shoulder mobility to improve my range of motion. I don’t count my steps, but I try to walk as much as I can throughout the day to keep my body moving and maintain cardiovascular health.

Feetures Elite Ultra Light Quarter Sock.

I love Feetures socks for their snug arch support and gentle compression that keeps them comfortably in place during workouts.

Clif Builders are my favorite post-workout snack since they taste great and pack 20 g of protein per bar.

When I first decided to work with a personal trainer in my 50s, I wanted guidance, accountability, and the confidence that I was exercising safely and effectively—and I got that. My first few trainers helped me build a foundation by teaching me proper form and the fundamental movements that I still rely on today.

Recent findings suggest that but working with Nate completely changed my relationship with lifting: He knows how to motivate me, pushing me without going beyond my abilities. When I attempt a fresh personal record, his belief in me helps me believe in myself, too. Now, I know what I’m capable of and how to challenge myself while lifting safely. The gym has become so much more than a place to work out—it’s where I keep discovering what I can do.

It has been revealed that I’ve learned that getting stronger isn’t just about how hard I work in the gym—it’s also about how well I recover between workouts through getting plenty of sleep, mobility work, stretching, and walking. When I don’t make time for recovery activities or I don’t fuel properly, it makes a difference; I feel more fatigued, have less energy during workouts, and struggle to perform at the same level.

Sources indicate that for me, progress doesn’t mean pushing myself to the limit every day. It means finding the right balance between challenging my body and giving it the rest and support it needs to keep getting stronger.

If you’d told me a few years ago that I’d be powerlifting in my 70s and chasing a deadlift record, I never would have believed you. Before I started training with Nate, I had never really set big fitness goals or thought about pushing my limits. But that began to change when I realized how much stronger I could become with the right coaching and encouragement. I was inspired to set goals that challenged me in latest ways I never thought possible, and I’ve learned that it’s never too late to surprise myself and try something new. Having a goal to work toward keeps me motivated, and I love seeing how far I can push myself when I have the right support and plan in place.

Of course, getting stronger takes patience, consistency, and a willingness to step outside my comfort zone, but the reward is so worth it. I hope my journey encourages other women, especially those in their 60s and 70s, to keep challenging themselves and try new things. They might discover a passion they never knew they had, just as I did.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prediction market traders see just a 14% chance of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia before the end of 2026, despite mounting pressure to reinstate the company's ousted co-founder.
  • 16, Polymarket traders priced Huang's chances of rejoining the artificial intelligence chipmaker by Nov.
  • The market has seen about $2.2 million in cumulative trading volume since opening on Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Prediction market traders see just a 14% chance of Jensen Huang returning to Nvidia before the end of 2026, despite mounting pressure to reinstate the company's ousted co-founder.

On Nov. 16, Polymarket traders priced Huang's chances of rejoining the artificial intelligence chipmaker by Nov. 30 at 6%, rising to 14% by Dec. 31 and 38% by the end of 2027.

The market has seen about $2.2 million in cumulative trading volume since opening on Nov. 12, showing growing speculation over the fate of one of Silicon Valley's most prominent executives.

However, the contracts measure whether Huang formally rejoins Nvidia in a corporate or governance capacity.

The relatively low near-term probabilities contrast with an increasingly public campaign for his reinstatement, which has attracted support from President Donald Trump, Tesla CEO Elon Musk and prominent institutional investors.

Huang resigned as Nvidia's chief executive, president and board member last week following revelations about extramarital relationships, including one with a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence.

The allegations have prompted an independent board investigation, although the espionage claims remain unproven.

Nvidia subsequently appointed longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO and began searching for a permanent replacement.

The campaign to bring Huang back gained momentum Monday after Trump publicly indicated that he would support his reinstatement.

He told reporters that he “would certainly not mind seeing that,” adding that Huang had “learned a major lesson.”.

The president also questioned the allegations involving the suspected Chinese intelligence operative, saying he did not know whether she was a spy and that Huang's relationship had not compromised US national security.

His intervention followed reports that Huang had discussed a possible return with close allies, some of whom were reportedly organizing a lobbying campaign to pressure Nvidia's board.

Meanwhile, an online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement has attracted more than 178,000 signatures, including names of prominent technology executives such as Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

Institutional shareholders have also entered the debate. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker urged Nvidia's board to keep all options open, including Huang's potential return, rather than rush into appointing a permanent successor.

Balaji Srinivasan, a prominent technology investor and former Coinbase executive, argued that Huang could mobilize enough shareholder support to challenge directors opposed to his reinstatement.

He suggested that Huang's influence at Nvidia and across the broader AI industry could push the board to reconsider its decision, citing provisions that allow qualifying shareholders to demand a special meeting.

“If Jensen indicates he wants back in, all of Nvidia and indeed the global AI ecosystem is still wired around him. The coup has no legitimacy. The anti-Jensen board members will immediately step down or likely be legally forced out.”.

In a recent development, yet shareholder support does not automatically translate into reinstatement. Nvidia's board retains responsibility for appointing a chief executive, and its investigation could significantly influence whether Huang is considered for another leadership role.

The next immediate test comes Nov. 17, when Nvidia reports quarterly earnings and holds its first major investor briefing since Huang's departure.

Investors will be looking for clarity on the company's leadership transition, strategic direction, and whether the board intends to consider its former chief executive as a potential successor.
