💡 Key Takeaways
  • The XRP Ledger’s proposed AMM V2 overhaul would let creators of automated trading pools choose how those pools price trades, potentially giving traders more usable liquidity for the same deposit.
  • The distinction is visible in today’s pools.
  • Recent findings suggest that those are reserve snapshots, not amounts a trader could exchange at an unchanged price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The XRP Ledger’s proposed AMM V2 overhaul would let creators of automated trading pools choose how those pools price trades, potentially giving traders more usable liquidity for the same deposit. For XRP holders, the potential benefits are better execution and newly introduced ways to provide liquidity; additional demand to hold the token would depend on which assets and routes attract capital.

The distinction is visible in today’s pools. XRPSCAN responses retrieved at 13:15 UTC on Nov. 15 revealed roughly 25,065 of Ripple’s dollar stablecoin RLUSD and 25,068 of Circle’s USDC in the RLUSD/USDC pool, about $50,133 if both stablecoins are valued at $1. The XRP/RLUSD pool held about 1.94 million XRP and 1.88 million RLUSD.

Recent findings suggest that those are reserve snapshots, not amounts a trader could exchange at an unchanged price. They also illustrate two different inventory needs: the first pair holds two stablecoins, while the second holds XRP.

CryptoSlate’s XRP page displayed $0.97 when retrieved at 13:15 UTC on Nov. 15, with market data marked as updated eight minutes earlier.

It has been revealed that an automated market maker, or AMM, lets customers trade against a pool whose prices follow a formula. XRPL’s current design uses a constant-product-style curve. Liquidity supports trading across a broad price range, even when the assets usually trade close to one another.

In a recent development, the AMM Swappable Curves draft proposes alternatives. StableSwap would concentrate effective depth near the expected relationship between correlated assets, such as two dollar stablecoins. Concentrated liquidity would let providers allocate capital within chosen price ranges. Binned liquidity would place assets at discrete fixed prices, with execution moving to another price when a funded bin is exhausted.

The economic aim is more executable depth per unit of capital. A stablecoin pool could serve trades near parity with less money spread across distant prices. A provider choosing a narrower range could make the same deposit more useful while that range remains active.

The size of any trading improvement would depend on funding, price ranges, fees, trade size and whether correlated assets remain close in value.

Routing matters as much as the curve. XRPL already combines AMMs and order books. The draft would compare curve offers at each routing step using their actual output after fees at the offer’s size, rather than choosing solely by the displayed marginal price. Any execution comparison must therefore include order-book liquidity and alternative routes, not just these two pools.

A more efficient direct RLUSD/USDC pool could improve stablecoin execution without holding XRP as either trading asset. Customers still face XRP transaction costs and applicable account or trust-line reserve requirements. Those requirements are separate from funding XRP inventory in a trading pair; current AMM ledger entries themselves have reserve exemptions, which do not automatically extend to upcoming position entries proposed for AMM V2.

An XRP pair creates a different opportunity because its inventory includes XRP. Even there, capital efficiency cuts both ways. Less XRP could support a given amount of executable depth, while a larger, more active market could attract enough providers to raise aggregate deposits.

In a recent development, proposed curves can change how efficiently liquidity works. The assets in each pair determine whether XRP is trading inventory.

A direct stablecoin pair can provide execution liquidity without XRP as a trading asset.

According to recent reports, an XRP pair includes XRP trading inventory. Larger pool balances alone do not establish additional market-wide holding demand.

Better execution can arrive without additional XRP holdings; adoption and persistent funding must be measured.

Industry observers note that AMM V2 is proposed. No efficiency multiple, executable quote, adoption forecast or upcoming XRP buying is established. XRP fees and applicable user reserves are separate from trading inventory.

Recent findings suggest that qualitative mechanism diagram from the draft specification and current AMM mechanics. Lines and circle sizes are schematic, not quoted prices, measured depth or proportional reserves. Pair choices show asset roles, not tested routes.

AMM V2 is proposed. No efficiency multiple, executable quote, adoption forecast or latest XRP buying is established. XRP fees and applicable user reserves are separate from trading inventory.

Higher turnover alone would not distinguish those outcomes. The same inventory can support repeated trades. A stronger holding-demand case would require persistent additional XRP balances across relevant pools and routes, with deposits, withdrawals and swaps separated so reserve changes are not mistaken for fresh buying.

Recent findings suggest that fee income also belongs to liquidity providers rather than all XRP holders. XRPL’s documentation describes relative-price and arbitrage risks. Concentrated liquidity adds range management: Uniswap’s explanation highlights how a position can become entirely one asset and stop earning fees outside its range. More efficient capital is not automatically more profitable capital.

Industry observers note that AMM V2 remains proposed work. The discussion opened in May, and the Foundation’s feasibility page was updated Nov. 4. Its roadmap lists rebasing and reopening the implementation pull request, then review and audit, as next steps. Activation requires validator approval. The current specification gives binned pools a separate amendment gate from concentrated liquidity and StableSwap.

It has been revealed that the Foundation’s Nov. 4 assessment said no issuer, wallet, exchange or DEX front end had publicly committed to using the pools.

For XRP holders, persistent inventory tied to additional funded use would strengthen the demand case, but larger pool balances alone could reflect capital moved from elsewhere. Better execution could arrive before any additional holding demand is demonstrated.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Perpetual futures exchange Lighter suspended withdrawals on Nov.
  • Bitquery traced 10.39 million USDC leaving its Ethereum contract, and Lighter stated in a subsequent enhancement that its investigation indicated a leaked API key for a specific trader's account caused the incident.
  • According to recent reports, it said the protocol and smart contracts were unaffected and that it was targeting a resumption of withdrawals by the end of Nov.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Perpetual futures exchange Lighter suspended withdrawals on Nov. 16 after a security incident that resulted in an estimated loss of roughly $15.5 million.

Bitquery traced 10.39 million USDC leaving its Ethereum contract, and Lighter stated in a subsequent enhancement that its investigation indicated a leaked API key for a specific trader's account caused the incident.

According to recent reports, it said the protocol and smart contracts were unaffected and that it was targeting a resumption of withdrawals by the end of Nov. 16.

According to Bitquery, the larger loss estimate concerns two market-maker accounts, which did not verify the internal account-loss allegations.

Sources indicate that bitquery identified one withdrawal of approximately 10,393,057 USDC on Nov. 16. The investigation separates that transfer from a second alleged loss of over $5 million. Bitquery says that if those funds left the second account, they had not left Lighter within its Ethereum observation window.

Bitquery's morning Ethereum trace follows one withdrawal through Lighter's contract.

The reported account loss does not establish how much left the exchange or how much can be recovered.

Internal account-loss allegations remain unverified. Ethereum data end around 12:13 UTC on Nov. 16; later movements and recovery are outside this trace.

In a recent development, qualitative boundary diagram using Bitquery's reported figures and transaction timestamp. Arrow indicates the observed withdrawal; shapes are not scaled to value. The reported dollar estimate is not a reconciled total of verified withdrawals. No derived arithmetic.

Internal account-loss allegations remain unverified. Ethereum data end around 12:13 UTC on Nov. 16; later movements and recovery are outside this trace.

Lighter's trades happen on its own rollup, which Bitquery indicates it does not read, so its Ethereum trace cannot verify every change to a trading account's balance.

According to Bitquery, five orders on the CoW Swap exchange converted 10.36 million USDC into Ethereum between 10:13 and 10:17 UTC.

Recent findings suggest that bitquery also traced twelve payments of 160 ETH and associated accounts on the Hyperliquid exchange buying the XMR1 token. The firm reported 3,845 ETH remaining in the recipient wallet at its 11:55 UTC snapshot.

It has been revealed that lighter noted it enabled what it calls Guardian mode and prioritized recovering funds involved in an additional withdrawal attempt. Its patch said withdrawals remained paused and that the Lighter Security Council would upgrade the contract.

The revision did not announce a recovered amount or a completed reopening, leaving both the eventual recovery and users' ability to withdraw separate from the funds already traced out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Hyundai IONIQ 5 remains one of America’s most popular EVs outside Tesla, with October sales up 21%.

While the Tesla Model Y and Model 3 still dominate the US electric vehicle market, accounting for about 50% of all sales through the third quarter, it was the Hyundai IONIQ 5 that ranked third.

The market has slowed since the $7,500 federal tax credit was removed last September, with several automakers reporting fewer EV sales than in 2025 when buyers rushed to claim the credit.

Hyundai responded by cutting prices on the 2026 IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims, with a new starting MSRP of around $35,000.

As the market shows signs of recovery, IONIQ 5 sales bounced back in October, rising 21% to 1,981 units.

Through the first 10 months of 2026, Hyundai sold 33,093 IONIQ 5s in the US, still down 23% from the more than 42,700 it sold during the same period last year, when credit was still available.

Hyundai said the IONIQ 5 helped drive growth as the company posted its best October in the US ever with 73,452 vehicles sold, a 5% increase YOY.

While Hyundai sold only 169 IONIQ 9s last month (-47%), sales are still up 49% through October, with nearly 6,700 units sold.

Hyundai’s hybrids set a upcoming October sales record, rising 20% from last year and accounting for 29% of total sales in October. Through October, Hyundai’s total US sales are up 3% YOY at 770,916 units.

Since not all automakers report monthly sales figures, it’s hard to determine where the IONIQ 5 stands through October.

Industry observers note that earlier today, Hyundai’s sister brand Kia reported that sales of its three-row electric SUV, the EV9, were up 11% year over year in October. EV9 sales are now up 5% year-to-date, with 13,835 units sold through October.

The cheapest 2027 Hyundai IONIQ 5 SE Standard Range starts at $35,250 and offers up to 245 miles of range.

If you want more range, upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, but you get up to 318 miles of range on a single charge.

Pennsylvania is way ahead on NEVI charging – now comes another $37M

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (598 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT indicates will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers.
  • The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties.
  • For drivers without a driveway, curbside charging gives them somewhere to plug in while parked near home.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT indicates will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers.

The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. PennDOT notes the projects will expand public charging availability by 27% across the region and 53% in Philadelphia.

For drivers without a driveway, curbside charging gives them somewhere to plug in while parked near home.

It’s Electric PA received $2.93 million for 157 on-street Level 2 ports across 13 Philadelphia neighborhoods. Voltpost received funding for another 62 curbside ports across the four suburban counties.

Fast charging is getting funding, too. PositivEnergy received $7.2 million for 54 DC fast-charging ports at 11 Philadelphia Parking Authority lots. Tesla received two $392,000 awards for eight ports each at Royal Farms in Broomall and Wawa in Plymouth Meeting.

The money comes from the federal National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, created by the Biden administration’s Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Pennsylvania’s five-year allocation is $171.5 million.

In a recent development, NEVI initially focused on fast charging along designated highway corridors. States can spend the money more broadly after the Federal Highway Administration certifies that their corridor charging requirements have been met. Pennsylvania received that certification on September 22, 2025.

In fact, Pennsylvania has built 54 EV charging stations using NEVI funds so far – more than double the number of any other state.

In a recent development, pennDOT’s community charging program supports both Level 2 and DC fast charging. Its published program minimum requirements include at least four ports per proposed station, at least 6 kW per port, two ADA-compliant parking spaces, and J1772 or CCS connectors on every port. Equipment must also meet Buy America requirements.

PennDOT lists 71 awards in this southeastern round as part of its roughly $100 million statewide community charging effort.

Applications for the western region close November 20. Central and eastern Pennsylvania applications close March 12, 2027.

thanks for posting. PA continues to lead the country in turning this program into actual chargers. The statewide coverage is night and day from just 2-3 years ago.

For the southeastern projects, PennDOT’s estimated schedule puts environmental reviews in November 2026 through January 2027, followed by agreement execution in January and February. Drivers will still have to wait for construction and commissioning before these awards become places to plug in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD wasted no time, with sales of its new flagship electric sedan reaching 4,000 in just 19 days since its launch.

With a record of more than 300,000 electric vehicles sold last month, BYD sold more EVs than the US did in the entire third quarter, combined.

A big part of the higher demand is thanks to BYD’s latest breakthrough technology, including its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.

BYD began equipping vehicles with the latest battery and charging tech in March, and over the past six months it has posted higher year-over-year sales growth. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 vehicles, up 6% compared to the same period in 2025.

On October 13, BYD introduced the Great Han, or “Da Han” in China, the first fully electric D-segment flagship sedan in its Dynasty lineup.

Industry observers note that just 19 days after its launch, BYD said Great Han EV sales reached 4,000 units. At that rate, sales could reach 10,000 or more in its first full month.

With “class-beating high value,” BYD said, “it has firmly established itself in the mid-to-high-end sedan segment above 250,000 yuan,” which is about $37,500.

It has been revealed that the Great Han is available in three variants, priced from 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000. Buyers can choose from single- or dual-motor powertrains. The standard rear-wheel-drive (RWD) Premium trim offers up to 1,008 km (626 miles) of CLTC range, while the all-wheel-drive (AWD) Flagship variant offers up to 880 km (546 miles).

All models use a 102.326 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery pack. The RWD models have a single 370 kW (496 hp) motor, while the AWD variant adds a 200 kW (268 hp) front motor for a combined 570 kW (764 hp).

Like most of its latest vehicles, the Great Han has a roof-mounted LiDAR and BYD’s God’s Eye B, a more advanced version of its intelligent driving system.

The ADAS system offers safety and convenience features, including Navigate on Autopilot on highways and in cities, plus remote autonomous parking.

All variants also include premium features, such as BYD’s DiSus-A dual-chamber air suspension system, rear-wheel steering, and zero-gravity front seats.

Industry observers note that measuring 5,256 mm in length, 1,999 mm in width, and 1,510 mm in height, with a 3,130 mm wheelbase, the Great Han is slightly bigger than the Tesla Model S and Lucid Air. It’s closer in size to the long-wheelbase Mercedes-Benz S-Class.

Thanks to BYD’s second-gen Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. A full recharge (10% to 97%) takes just 9 minutes.

The Great Han joins the Great Tang SUV as the flagship sedan under BYD’s Dynasty lineup. BYD unveiled that Great Tang sales reached 14,000 units in October, marking four months of sales above 10,000.

#5744. Industry News: What does a blue Texas sweep mean for Elon Musk, Tesla & SpaceX?

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1415 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: What does a blue Texas sweep mean for Elon Musk, Tesla & SpaceX?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1415 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue.
  • The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.
  • In a recent development, perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning every statewide contest.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies.

The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.

In a recent development, perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning every statewide contest. Republicans maintained some state legislative power and won the State Senate, but as of this writing Democrats are right now ahead in the count for the State House.

It has been revealed that the highest profile contest was for Texas Senate, where James Talarico won by a 55-43 margin. This race set the record for the most expensive Senate race in the nation’s history, with over half a billion dollars spent on this one seat alone.

In a recent development, about half of the total money spent on the race came courtesy of republican PACs, a method by which companies and the ultra-wealthy can launder money into bribes to buy elections. And most of the PAC money in the race came from one man, Elon Musk, who spent $212 million to support the enormously unpopular and scandal-ridden outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton.

Sources indicate that that’s nearly half of the $474 million dollars that Musk put into this election cycle, suggesting that he saw this race of particular importance. And yet, his candidate lost miserably.

But the rout did not stop with Paxton. Paxton’s old job as AG is now going to be filled by Democrat Nathan Johnson. And Greg Abbott, the outgoing Governor, was defeated by Gina Hinojosa. Even the less high-profile races for court seats were swept by Democrats – three seats on the 15th Court of Appeals and four seats on the Texas Supreme Court.

And those results, even beyond the big-spending Senate race, could all matter quite a lot to Elon Musk.

In 2021, Musk announced that Tesla would move its headquarters to Texas, after Musk got in a spat with California government because he didn’t want to follow COVID restrictions for worker safety.

But the move wasn’t only about COVID restrictions – it was also about Musk’s vision of having more control over the business environment. And, by making allies with Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott, he has had quite a bit of control in Texas.

The two have rolled out the red carpet for Musk, giving him carte blanche in his adopted state.

Sources indicate that autonomous vehicle regulations have been changed, allowing driverless Robotaxis to operate where other states with more advanced regulations and transparency requirements would not. And many other laws benefitting Tesla and SpaceX have been passed. Paxton even sued Sam Altman, Musk’s chief AI rival, just weeks ago.

Perhaps more notably for Musk personally, Texas has promised to allow Musk to get away with more financial shenanigans than states with more established business regulations might.

In a recent development, with Tesla both headquartered and incorporated in Texas, it can now use special “business courts” instituted by Abbott at Musk’s own urging. If cases from these courts are appealed, they go to the 15th Court of Appeals, a court created by Abbott and filled with 3 hand-picked judges, intended to reduce the chance that a Democratic district court (say, one in Austin, whereTesla is headquartered) gets final say on any concern.

But, the 15th Court of Appeals just had elections last night – and its three seats were flipped to Democratic control.

The 15th Court of Appeals also, just last week, stopped an inquiry into thousands of pages of emails between Abbott and Musk. The emails had been released, but are heavily redacted, with Abbott referring to the redacted portions as having “intimate” information in them.

It has been revealed that and who made that request for inquiry into the emails? Gina Hinojosa, a name you might recognize, as she is the next Governor of Texas, as of last night.

It has been revealed that as of yet, those emails have not all been released, so we don’t actually know exactly how much influence Musk was able to exercise over the state’s outgoing Governor. But given the changes we know about, the money Musk spent in Texas, and the thousands of pages of emails that have been redacted, it seems likely that there is something more to be found in them.

So what does this all mean for Tesla, our main area of coverage here at Electrek?

On a Texas state level, probably not all that much. There’s no reason that Democrats in the state would interfere with Tesla’s production of electric vehicles – in fact, they’d probably encourage it more than republicans do. Talarico has stated that he supports Tesla – it is a large employer in the state, after all.

And certainly, the national wins by Democrats could be a boon for EVs, and for climate action, given how hostile republicans have been to them (and Musk has been the single largest supporter of that hostility towards EVs, which has cost Tesla billions).

Sources indicate that the same likely goes for SpaceX – perhaps a blue Texas will be more restrictive of the firm’s improper usage of protected habitats, or building of data centers, or whatever the hell is going on on twitter. But the core businesses of space rolls out and Starlink don’t seem likely to go anywhere.

For Elon Musk, though, things could be different. Given his “intimate” relationship with Abbott, the extreme amounts of money he spent on Paxton, and the highly personal nature of his truly ridiculous attacks against Talarico, it seems unlikely that he will have a similar level of allyship with Texas government actors as he did in prior years. Talarico’s main anti-corruption message was seemingly aimed straight at Musk’s attempts to buy elections, after all.

And given his high levels of spending on a party that is outright hostile electric vehicles, it seems clear that his personal fortunes are far more important to him than the well-being of his companies.

In a recent development, as a texan, I had zero faith that talrico would win, especially with the amount of money musk dumped in the race at the last minute. I’m so heartened to see that money cannot buy everything and that we, as a country, are finally pushing back against the trump/musk insanity. maybe we can start upholding the constitution and ensuring the law applies to all citizens regardless of wealth.

It has been revealed that this is all notable to note, because Musk has been working towards a scheme to merge SpaceX and Tesla, a deal which would likely be a detriment to both companies and all of their shareholders. Musk wants the deal so he can exercise more control over, and extract more personal wealth from, the combined entity.

But that scheme could rely on a favorable legal environment in Texas courts, an environment that just got less favorable.

Industry observers note that and, given Musk’s penchant for childish lashings-out anytime he deems people insufficiently obsequious to his imagined greatness, could we see another situation where Musk encounters the tiniest amount of pushback from state government and then picks up his toys and leaves, as he already did in both California and Delaware? Time will have to tell. Keep your popcorn buckets primed and ready.

#5739. Tesla accused of selling FSD to Korean owners who can’t legally use it

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (886 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla accused of selling FSD to Korean owners who can’t legally use it

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (886 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it.
  • Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it.
  • In a recent development, it all comes down to where the car was built.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year.

Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD.

In a recent development, it all comes down to where the car was built. The Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck come from US factories and enter Korea under the KORUS free trade agreement, which recognizes US safety standards. Those are the only Teslas that got “FSD (Supervised)” when Tesla switched it on in Korea late last year.

The problem is that those don’t represent the vast majority of Tesla vehicles sold in Korea.

Industry observers note that the Model 3 and Model Y sold in Korea come from Giga Shanghai. There’s no equivalent deal with China, so those cars need Korean approval that FSD doesn’t have.

Sources indicate that and that’s most of the fleet. Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk told lawmakers last month that FSD works on about 20% of Teslas registered in the country. Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-built vehicles in Korea since 2023, per data it handed to the National Assembly, and sales of those China-made cars grew more than fivefold between 2023 and 2025.

In a recent development, seo’s figure also clears up the conflicting eligibility numbers we flagged when Korean police booked 80 Tesla drivers for using illegal FSD unlock devices last month. A lawmaker’s data from May put it at 2.4%, while a data firm counted 20.7% in August. Tesla’s own testimony matches the higher one.

According to recent reports, for years, Tesla charged Korean buyers a one-time 9.043 million won (about $6,726) for FSD. It moved to a 150,000 won ($112) monthly subscription in August.

Industry observers note that the complaint points to Tesla’s “coming soon” promotion last year and a demo video shot on Korean roads. Neither made it clear that FSD would only work on a small slice of the cars Tesla was selling. The group says Tesla knew that and kept pitching the package to every buyer anyway.

“Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day,” noted Choi Young-suk, who heads automotive complications at the group.

It wants the KFTC to temporarily order Tesla to stop marketing FSD for ineligible cars. It’s also asking for fines and for the case to be sent to state investigators.

Industry observers note that the KFTC is already looking at this. An official told Reuters the agency opened a probe into Tesla’s FSD advertising earlier this year and has received written responses from the tech giant. Tesla didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.

Sources indicate that tesla has collected FSD money from buyers of China-made cars in Korea for more than three years. But at an October 8 parliamentary hearing, Seo testified that Tesla had never formally asked the transport ministry to test FSD. Tesla filed for certification about two weeks later.

According to recent reports, approval won’t be a rubber stamp either. The ministry told a lawmaker that FSD doesn’t comply with local safety rules, including the requirement that drivers keep their hands on the wheel. Current FSD versions let drivers go hands-free as long as the cabin camera sees them watching the road.

None of this slowed sales. Tesla passed BMW this year to become Korea’s top imported car brand.

In a recent development, so far, owners haven’t had much luck in court. Last month, a Seoul court dismissed a lawsuit from Tesla owners seeking FSD refunds, with the judge pointing to Korean regulations, not Tesla, as the reason more features never launched.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kia is crushing it with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from entry-level SUVs to the three-row EV9 and PV5 van.
  • With 291,219 vehicles sold last month, up 10.3% from October 2025, Kia posted its eighth consecutive month of year-over-year sales growth.
  • Kia said it plans to build on the momentum by focusing on electrified vehicles in key markets, including hybrids in the US and fully electric vehicles in Europe.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Kia is crushing it with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from entry-level SUVs to the three-row EV9 and PV5 van. A leaked document revealed that Kia aims to add the EV7, a fresh midsize electric SUV, to fill the gap between the EV6 and the three-row EV9.

With 291,219 vehicles sold last month, up 10.3% from October 2025, Kia posted its eighth consecutive month of year-over-year sales growth.

Kia said it plans to build on the momentum by focusing on electrified vehicles in key markets, including hybrids in the US and fully electric vehicles in Europe.

After launching the EV2 earlier this year, Kia now offers one of the most complete EV lineups, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van.

According to a recently leaked document, a new midsize electric SUV will join the lineup. KoreanCarBlog uncovered an internal document from Kia’s Employment Stability Committee that reveals the organization’s upcoming production plans.

The report claims “production of mid-range electric SUV ‘EV7’ to proceed” at Kia’s Gwangju factory in South Korea.

Although no other details were revealed, the EV7 will be a midsize electric SUV, slotted between the EV6 and three-row EV9.

During its 2026 CEO Investor Day in April, Kia announced aims to expand its EV lineup to 14 models by 2030.

In Europe, Kia plans for EVs to account for 66% of sales by 2030, with a full lineup that includes the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, three PBVs, a new C-segment electric SUV, and its first “SDV B-segment hatchback.”.

According to recent reports, so what can we expect from the upcoming EV7? Kia said earlier this year that it’s developing a new EV platform “to significantly enhance both product performance and cost competitiveness.”.

Although it didn’t offer specifics, Kia claimed the new EV platform delivers up to a 40% increase in battery capacity and a 9% improvement in motor output.

It will use Kia’s fifth-generation batteries, providing up to 15% higher energy density than its current tech.

Kia’s upcoming software-defined vehicles (SDVs) are expected to integrate Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.They will also have Level 2++ autonomous driving capabilities on highways.

The EV5, Kia’s current midsize electric SUV, is 4,615 mm long, 1,875 mm wide, and 1,675 mm tall, with a 2,750 mm wheelbase, which is about the size of the Sportage, so you can expect the EV7 to be slightly bigger. It will likely be closer in size to the Sorento.

Powered by an 81.4 kWh battery, the Kia’s current EV5 offers a WLTP range of up to 329 miles (530 km).

Sources indicate that not a full lineup, the EV van is still missing. Why offer so many different SUVs between Kia and Hyundai but no van/minivan?

Recent findings suggest that however, unlike the EV6 and EV9, the EV5 uses a 400V electrical architecture rather than an 800V. As a result, charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes, rather than 18 to 25 minutes. The upcoming EV7 will likely use the 800V system for faster charging.

The document also revealed Kia will begin production of “completely redesigned models” at its Gwangmyeong Factory, including the 2028 Carnival Hybrid and a hydrogen-powered Carnival by 2029.

At its Gyeonggi Hwaseong Factory, Kia will reportedly also produce redesigned models, including the Sorento Hybrid in 2028.

#5734. Industry News: Puerto Rico tapped Sunrun’s home batteries for 18 straight days

Industry News: Puerto Rico tapped Sunrun’s home batteries for 18 straight days

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (646 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October.
  • A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.
  • It has been revealed that sunrun says its VPP network in Puerto Rico now includes nearly 70,000 batteries, frequently delivering 45 megawatts (MW) for four hours at a time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October.

A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.

It has been revealed that sunrun says its VPP network in Puerto Rico now includes nearly 70,000 batteries, frequently delivering 45 megawatts (MW) for four hours at a time. It has dispatched them more than 60 times since April, including daily deployments beginning October 13 during unusually hot weather.

For Puerto Ricans, who pay some of the highest electricity prices in the US, getting reliable power for all that money remains a problem. Residential electricity averaged 26.36 cents per kilowatt-hour in August, compared with a US average of 18.16 cents, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).

That makes the batteries already installed at homes pretty useful. The grid can pay to tap their stored energy when supplies get tight, putting existing equipment to work without waiting for a newly introduced power plant to be built.

In a recent development, sunrun’s network grew from around 4,000 customers in 2024 to more than 30,000 in 2025. It indicates it’s the largest aggregator in Puerto Rico’s Customer Battery Energy Sharing (CBES) program.

Industry observers note that LUMA, the island’s grid operator, calls on CBES when it expects electricity demand or reserve needs to exceed available generation. Companies such as Sunrun then manage the battery response automatically.

Homeowners get paid for sharing energy and choose how much to keep for backup. Sunrun notes most share a small portion of their total battery capacity; the company earns recurring revenue for operating the network.

Across the wider CBES program, LUMA reported in July that more than 90,000 participating customers had helped provide an average of 75 MW during generation shortfalls.

Puerto Rico’s reliability problem goes well beyond hurricanes.

Customers averaged 36 hours without power in 2025, even excluding major events, according to the US EIA. That’s up 19% from 2024. Mainland US customers generally experience about two hours a year under the same measure. Major events added another 23 hours of outages on the island.

In a recent development, more batteries can help, but the size of the shortfall still matters. In an April regulatory filing, participating aggregators remarked the program couldn’t prevent every rolling blackout in 2025 because some supply gaps exceeded its roughly 50 MW of four-hour capacity. They’re looking to enroll more batteries so the program can cover larger shortfalls.

#5731. Xiaomi’s humanoid robots work a full 8-hour shift in its EV factory

EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Xiaomi’s humanoid robots work a full 8-hour shift in its EV factory

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1041 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xiaomi has released footage of its humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift at its EV factory, sorting center console side covers for its cars.
  • If that’s fully autonomous, it’s truly impressive.
  • Xiaomi Tech posted the video on X on November 3, as the manufacturer picked up awards at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xiaomi has released footage of its humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift at its EV factory, sorting center console side covers for its cars. The company says the robots did it on their own, catching and fixing their own mistakes along the way.

If that’s fully autonomous, it’s truly impressive. But we’ve been disappointed by humanoid robot demos before, and Xiaomi left out the numbers that would let anyone check.

Xiaomi Tech posted the video on X on November 3, as the manufacturer picked up awards at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen. It shows the robots pulling side covers from bins, carrying them to storage racks, and placing them into slots, with a running clock of cumulative working time and an “Autonomous, 100x Speed” label in the corner.

8 hours on the production line. 🤖Xiaomi’s full-size humanoid robot takes on an 8-hour task at the Center Console Side-Cover Sorting Workstation at Xiaomi Auto Factory.Beyond sustained operation, it can autonomously detect and correct anomalies while coordinating with the… pic.twitter.com/brpO3S5bCn.

It has been revealed that according to Xiaomi, the robot covered the full day of production needs at that workstation. The company indicates it detected and corrected anomalies on its own and coordinated with the production line’s control system, calling it “another step toward real-world industrial deployment.”.

This is the third milestone in a program Xiaomi has been running in public all year. In March, it put a humanoid in its Beijing EV factory as an “intern” installing self-tapping nuts. Xiaomi reported a 90.2% success rate over three hours, fast enough to meet the station’s 76-second cycle time. By July, it noted that success rate was up to 98%, and it added two harder stations, including the side-cover sorting job from this week’s video.

Last December, Xiaomi’s CEO, Lei Jun, said the firm aims to deploy humanoid robots in large numbers across its factories within five years.

Xiaomi also announced that its open-source Xiaomi-Robotics-1 AI model, pre-trained on 100,000 hours of real-world robot data, has started trial runs in Xiaomi staff apartments. In a 30-minute run, it completed more than 50 task chains across three rooms.

Xiaomi didn’t say how many parts the robots sorted, what the success rate was over eight hours, or how many times a human had to step in. It also didn’t explain how the robots stayed powered for a full shift: swapped batteries, a tether, or charging breaks.

Sources indicate that and that matters, because “autonomous” in a robot video can mean anything. Tesla’s Optimus robots at the 2024 “We, Robot” event were remotely operated by humans, which Tesla didn’t disclose at the time. Last December, an Optimus took a suspicious tumble in a Miami demo, raising its hands to its head like a teleoperator pulling off a VR headset as it fell.

Sources indicate that to be fair to Xiaomi, it has published success rates and cycle times for its earlier factory tests. That’s more than Tesla has ever shared about Optimus doing useful work, and Tesla now claims it won’t deliver Optimus to outside customers until late 2027.

In a recent development, the most interesting moment in the video comes around the 1:37 mark. In a segment Xiaomi labels “Dropped Material: Multi-Robot Collaboration,” a humanoid upper body mounted on a wheeled base rolls in to help the two legged robots.

Recent findings suggest that it’s not the only thing on wheels in that scene, either. The bins of parts are shuttled around by autonomous mobile robots, the same kind of wheeled platforms that have been moving materials in car factories for years.

According to recent reports, they could have got a lot more done if they'd moved the parts bins closer so the bots didn't have to walk as far. That's a huge open space between the two.

If this demo was truly fully autonomous for eight hours, with the robots handling their own errors, that’s one of the more impressive humanoid demos we’ve seen. Xiaomi deserves credit for putting its robots on a real production line and publishing some real numbers along the way. But we’ve been burned by “autonomous” robot demos before, so we’ll wait for more details before getting too excited.

Sources indicate that the wheeled robot is our favorite part of the video, though. It’s a great example of why you shouldn’t bet everything on the humanoid form factor. Wheels are far more efficient than legs on most terrain, and a flat factory floor is the best-case scenario for wheels. A wheeled base doesn’t burn energy just to stay upright, it’s more stable when carrying parts, it has room for a much bigger battery (which would solve that 8-hour power question), and it needs fewer expensive actuators.

Sources indicate that the value in these robots is in the hands, arms, and the AI driving them. Legs make sense in homes with stairs, and maybe that’s where Xiaomi wants to take them eventually. But factories were designed around carts and forklifts, not people walking around carrying parts.

Industry observers note that as robots and AI put more strain on the grid and electricity rates climb, solar and batteries are becoming essential home infrastructure, not a luxury. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • The slide has been punishing for leveraged traders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, bitcoin price traded near $64,000 on Monday morning, down about 2% from Sunday, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The world’s largest cryptocurrency is trying to hold its ground after a weekend plunge to $62,000, as tech stocks slid ahead of Nvidia’s earnings and traders braced for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

The selling that broke Friday’s low on Saturday morning did not stop there. Bitcoin slipped under $64,000 Saturday afternoon and dropped below $62,000 in the 8 p.m. ET hour on some exchanges, its lowest level since July 14. It bounced back above $64,800 within the hour and reached about $66,100 early Sunday before sellers returned. The bitcoin price has spent most of the past day between $64,000 and $65,000.

The slide has been punishing for leveraged traders. About $2 billion of crypto positions were liquidated over a 24-hour period during the weekend, the vast majority of them long bets. Bitcoin is now down 17% in November and has posted six straight weekly losses.

According to recent reports, stock futures offered little help on Monday. Contracts on the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.5% and S&P 500 futures slipped 0.7%, while Nvidia fell 3% in premarket trading. Investors weighed a Financial Times report that former CEO Jensen Huang and his allies are discussing a campaign to reinstate him, a week after his resignation sent bitcoin below $72,000.

Nvidia reports third-quarter results on Tuesday, and options markets imply an earnings-day move of about 7% in either direction, Pepperstone’s Chris Weston told Reuters. Bitcoin has traded in step with chip stocks for much of the past week, so a weak report could add to the pressure.

Rates remain the other weight on the bitcoin price. Traders fully price a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s December meeting, with odds of a half-point move near 8%, CME FedWatch data show. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 5.12% on Monday after jumping 29 basis points last week, and higher yields have lifted the dollar to its strongest level since April 2025. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in San Francisco later Monday, and minutes from the last Fed meeting are due Wednesday.

Bitcoin-linked stocks fell with the coin. Strategy (MSTR) was down 8% in premarket trading and Strive (ASST) fell 9%. Strategy is also facing index-fund selling after MSCI removed it from its USA index, forcing index funds to sell by Nov. 30.

Sources indicate that spot bitcoin ETFs shed another $185 million on Friday, their seventh straight day of outflows, bringing losses since Nov. 5 to about $1.91 billion. That run follows BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) bleeding $2 billion over nine straight sessions.

In a recent development, analysts are now focused on the $60,000 level, which marked the lows of February and June. John Roque, technical strategist at 22V Research, mentioned bitcoin is close to completing a head-and-shoulders top. “Bitcoin has not broken below its neckline at 60,000,” he wrote in a note Saturday, adding that such a breach “would then imply risk to $38,000.”.

Matt Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak + Co., wrote that bitcoin “NEEDS to hold the $60k level,” warning that “any material break below that level would be quite bearish.” A gauge of bitcoin’s 30-day implied volatility climbed to 49.75 over the weekend, its highest since June.

It has been revealed that with Nvidia’s report, Fed speakers and the Fed minutes all due in the next three days, the bitcoin price faces a busy week. A move back above $66,000 would recover Sunday’s bounce high, while a break below the weekend low near $62,000 would put the $60,000 floor in play.

At the time of writing, the bitcoin price is near $64,100.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Mel Robbins has always been a mover—running, hiking, skiing, Pilates, yoga, you name it—but it’s only been recently that the 58-year-old has added strength training to her fitness regimen. She credits Dr. Stacy Sims (a Women’s Health advisory board member) and Dr. Vonda Wright, both guests on The Mel Robbins Podcast, with finally persuading her to lift weights.

Sources indicate that “They kept saying, when we reach a certain age, 40 and up, for us to start resistance training and with heavier weights,” claims Mel, who had to overcome a few fitness myths to finally prioritize pumping iron. “I was nervous I would bulk up. That's a joke, because you know how much you need to train to actually bulk up? I wasn't going to be doing that.”.

In a recent development, so what exactly does Mel do in the gym? She walked WH through a typical session for the latest episode of Strong Like.

Before Mel’s feet ever touch a mat, she makes sure to jot down—with actual pen and paper!—what she intends to do at the gym. “This will ensure that you actually do it, because if you're relying on this noggin up here, it ain't happening,” she states.

With her to-do list by her side, Mel begins her session with a warm-up. She runs through a batter of stretches that include inchworms (with an added push-up—go Mel!) and lunges with a twist, before moving on to a banded overhead press to mobilize her shoulders. “I've stopped judging these little bands,” Mel says. “These little suckers look like nothing. Let me tell you, there's a whole lot of something in these bands. You'll be shocked at how much gain you can get and how great this is for you.”.

With her warm-up complete, she moves on to the workout, shifting the bands from her arms to her legs for a duck walk. Mimicking the water fowl, she moves forward and back, side to side, keeping outward pressure on the bands.

Next, she tackles one of her favorite moves, a reverse lunge with medicine ball twist. “It's a compound movement that works mobility, your core, your arms, your legs, everything in one movement,” Mel says. “It's super-simple, painful, and awful, and it works like a charm.”.

She moves on to the upper body with chest presses, though she has a hack for lighting up even more muscles in the process. “If you want to maximize what you're doing here, suck in your stomach and clench your butt, because then it's not just arms; it's a whole-body thing,” she says.

Finally, she concludes with a snatch, joking: “You can work out a lot of aggression at the world doing [these].”.

It has been revealed that ultimately, states Mel, her approach to fitness is pretty straightforward: “I'm not in here because I want to look good in a bathing suit. I do, but that's not the motivation. I'm in here lifting weights because I want to live a long, vibrant, healthy life. I want to be dancing into my late 90s. I want to make sure I can pick up the suitcase and put it up in the overhead. I want to make sure that I am strong so my life is long.”.

Tech Report: The 7 Best Wired Headphones for Your Runs and Workouts

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2531 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Menshealth

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved.
  • Recent findings suggest that WIRED HEADPHONES ARE popular again.
  • You'll never get to the gym and find out your headphones are dead, and a pair that's been sitting in your bag for a month still works as soon as you plug it in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Recent findings suggest that WIRED HEADPHONES ARE popular again. The cords are showing up in NBA arena tunnels, where Golden State Warriors point guard Steph Curry walks in with them hanging from his ears. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams wears corded headphones as part of his pregame routine. Bose felt they were worth bringing back, too. In October, it started shipping the $99 Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds, its first upcoming wired headphones in years.While our favorite wireless workout headphones are more advanced than ever, they still have problems at the gym: connections drop, audio crackles, and you have to constantly manage the battery. And we've all had a bud knocked loose by a burpee and watched it bounce across the floor and under a squat rack. Just me? A wired pair avoids all of that. Sound travels through the cable, so there are no Bluetooth dropouts, and if a bud slips out, it hangs from the cord instead of hitting the ground.

Wired earbuds also have no battery. You'll never get to the gym and find out your headphones are dead, and a pair that's been sitting in your bag for a month still works as soon as you plug it in.

Sure, the cord can have its own drawbacks. It can snag on a rack in the gym, and when you run, it can bounce around into your body and arms. Its weight also pulls the buds downward, which can put pressure on your ears.

It has been revealed that most picks below have a way to keep the buds in place, including ear hooks, stabilizer wings, or a cable that runs over the top of your ear. Most also come with the right plug for your phone, so you don’t need an adapter. These are the best wired headphones you can get right now.

In a recent development, the Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds are the only pair on this list with active noise canceling. Each bud has two microphones that pick up the clang of plates and the music on the gym speakers, then cancel that sound. With the room quieter, you can keep your own music at a lower volume. Hold the button on the inline remote to switch to Aware mode. It uses the same mics to pipe in outside sound, so you can hear cars and cyclists on an outdoor run.

Noise canceling works best when each bud seals your ear canal, and silicone wing-tip stabilizers keep that seal in place while you move. Bose’s wings press against the inner ridge of your ear, so the buds don't shift during jumps or sprints. You get two wing sizes and three ear tip sizes, and you can remove the wings if you don't need them. The thick, rubbery 4.2-foot cable connecting them is durable. It tangles less than the thin cords on cheap USB-C buds, and it makes less noise when it rubs against a shirt.

In a recent development, partway down that cable sits the remote, which holds volume buttons, a multifunction button (tap to play or pause, double-tap to skip, hold to change noise modes), and the call mic. All that hardware can be heavy, though — enough that you'll feel it pull on the buds during jumps and sprints. Running the cable under your shirt collar keeps the remote from swinging.

The noise canceling also determines what you can plug these into. The earbuds draw power from your phone to run the mics and processor, so they need a USB-C port. Any iPhone 15 or newer works, and most current Android phones do too. A 3.5mm jack, like the one on a treadmill screen or an airplane seat, won't work, even with an adapter. Once they're plugged in, the IPX4 rating protects them from sweat and splashes from any direction, though not from a dunk in water. They come in black, white, and a limited-edition mint.

Read more: Best Workout Headphones, Tested by Us.

According to recent reports, the JBL Endurance Run 3 costs $25 and carries an IP65 rating, the highest on this list. That means no dust gets in on dirt trails and sandy beach runs, while they can survive water sprayed from a nozzle. A downpour or a sweat-soaked HIIT class won't hurt them, either.

Recent findings suggest that JBL's FlipHook design gives you two ways to wear them. With the cable hanging straight down, they sit like regular earbuds. Rotate the hooks upward and the cable runs over the top of your ear and down behind it. That takes the cable's weight off the bud. It also stops the wire from thumping against your chest while you run and jump. The TwistLock tips sit into the bowl of your ear, so a bud stays put when you turn your head fast.

Sources indicate that the remote has one button and a mic, handling play, pause, and calls, and a long press brings up Siri or Google Assistant. You can adjust the volume through your phone. The standard Run 3 plugs into a 3.5mm jack. JBL also offers the Endurance Run 3C USB-C, which has a three-button remote and costs a little more. The standard Endurance Run 3 has a 3.5mm plug and a one-button remote.

The MEE Audio M6 Sport uses memory wire, a thin, bendable wire inside the cable near each bud. You bend it around the back of your ear once, and it holds that curve. It works like a custom-fit ear hook that stays put through box jumps and hill sprints, and it also takes stress off the buds.

The three-button remote on the braided cable does more than most wired sport buds. The outer buttons raise and lower volume. The center button plays, pauses, skips tracks, answers calls, and starts your voice assistant. The IPX5 rating protects against heavy sweat and rain.

According to recent reports, MEE Audio tunes the M6 Sport for heavy bass. The USB-C version works with modern smartphones, and it comes with a shirt clip and six sets of ear tips, so you can get the exact fit you want. You can also get them a with a 3.5mm jack plug..

The SE215 earphones are in-ear monitors, the same style of earphones musicians wear on stage to hear themselves over a loud crowd. The low-profile shells sit flush inside your ear. The cable runs up and over the back of each ear, pulling the cord's weight off the buds and keeping cable noise out of your music when you move. The included foam tips expand to fill your ear canal, and Shure notes they block up to 37 decibels of outside noise, enough to drown out a gym's speakers.

Industry observers note that the SE215 delivers deeper bass than other wired headphones we’ve tested. Beyond sound, the earbuds have also been designed with durability in mind. The SE215's cable is Kevlar-reinforced and detaches at MMCX connectors, so if it breaks, you only replace the cord. Shure also sells a Bluetooth adapter that makes the same buds wireless.

In a recent development, shure doesn't give them an IP rating, though, so you should wipe them down after sweaty sessions. The standard 64-inch cable has no mic or remote and comes only in a 3.5mm configuration, so a USB-C phone needs a dongle.

Apple’s EarPods are the pair you see a lot of people using in TikTok videos, holding the mic close to their mouth. At $19, they’re a great pair to keep in your bag for the day you forget your main headphones. The remote has volume buttons and a center button to play, pause, and answer calls. Apple says they're protected against sweat and water, though it doesn't list an IP rating.

Sources indicate that the EarPods have hard plastic shells shaped to rest in the bowl of your ear, with no silicone tips sealing the canal. That makes them comfortable for long walks and lets outside sound in. But nothing holds them in place for more rigorous movements like burpees and jump rope. Still, they're steady enough for walking, the elliptical, and light lifting.

Read more: Our Review of the Apple iPhone Duo.

According to recent reports, the Avantree C171’s ear hooks are molded to curve over and behind each ear, so unlike the MEE Audio M6 Sport, no wire needs to be bent into shape. The cable runs down behind your ear instead of hanging from the bud, so it’s more out of the way when you’re moving.

A four-button remote controls volume, playback, calls, and your voice assistant, so you can keep your phone in your pocket. Avantree sells similar sport earbuds with USB-C, Lightning, and 3.5mm plugs; the C171 is the USB-C model, and the brand’s C171 manual includes troubleshooting for Galaxy S24 users who run into audio detection or distortion issues.

They don’t have an IP rating, but if fit is your main concern, these shouldn’t fly out of your ear during a HIIT workout.

The Avantree Resolve's speakers rest just outside your ear canal instead of sealing inside it, so you can still hear traffic and cyclists coming up behind you on a run. With no tip pressing into your ear canal, you'll also feel less soreness that builds up over a long session.

Sources indicate that since nothing sits inside your ear to hold the speakers in place, flexible hooks wrap over each ear to hold them in place. That grip won't be as snug as an in-ear tip, so the speakers can shift more when you move. Avantree makes a Small-Medium size for ears under 2.5 inches long and a Large size for everyone else, so measure your ear before you order.

While there is no IP rating, you do get inline remote controls for playback, volume, calls, and your voice assistant. Avantree sells 3.5mm, USB-C, and Lightning versions.

Wired headphones are better if your workouts keep getting cut short by dead batteries or bad Bluetooth connections. Without a battery, wired headphones play as soon as you plug them in, no matter how long they've sat unused. There's also no battery to wear out after two or three years of charging, which is when many wireless earbuds start dying mid-run.

Recent findings suggest that wireless buds are the better choice when you need total freedom of movement. Rolling on the floor, kipping pull-ups, and jump rope can all snag a cord. If your workouts are mostly lifting, steady running, or cardio machines, a cord rarely gets in the way.

Sources indicate that like any earbud, whether it’s wired or wireless, they can fall out of your ear. The cable's weight pulls on each bud with every step, so look for one of three fixes: ear hooks, like the memory wire on the MEE Audio M6 Sport or the FlipHook on the JBL Endurance Run 3, loop the cable over your ear. Stability wings, like those on the Bose, brace the bud against the ridge inside your ear. Over-ear cable routing, as on the Shure SE215, takes the cable's weight off the bud entirely. Plain earbuds with no tips or wings, like Apple's EarPods, are the most likely to fall out.

Yes, if you match the plug to your phone. USB-C earbuds plug straight into an iPhone 15 and later and most Android phones. Their digital-to-analog converter is built into the plug or cable, so you don't need an adapter. Since most modern smartphones no longer have a 3.5mm jack, earbuds with a 3.5mm plug need a USB-C-to-3.5mm dongle, and on a run that dongle adds weight and can snag on equipment. Choose a USB-C version when one exists.

The thumping you hear when the cord bounces against your shirt is called microphonic. Vibration travels up the wire into the earbud. Routing the cable over your ears is the most effective fix because it breaks the straight path from your chest to your ear canal. Running the cable under your shirt collar also stops it from swinging. A thicker, rubberized cable, like Bose's, transmits less noise than a thin plastic one.

In a recent development, IPX4 is the minimum for sweaty workouts. An IP rating has two digits. The first is dust protection on a scale up to 6, and the second is water protection on a scale up to 9. An X means the product wasn't tested for that category. IPX4 protects against splashing water from any direction, which covers sweat. An IPX5 rating means the headphones can withstand water jets, but it doesn’t guarantee protection in every condition, such as heavy rain. IP65, the JBL Endurance Run 3's rating, adds full dust protection for trail running.

Industry observers note that water and dust resistance is one area where wireless earbuds are well ahead. Most wireless workout models are rated at least IPX4, and many are rated IP55 or higher. Only three of the wired picks here have a rating: the Bose, the JBL, and the MEE Audio. If your pair doesn't have one, they can still survive light sweat, but remember to wipe them dry after each session.

According to recent reports, I use Apple’s EarPods every day and have spent years testing wireless headphones and earbuds. That experience shaped what I looked for here. For this guide, I picked models based on factors like fit, durability, compatibility, and inline controls. The rest of the Men's Health team also reviewed and contributed to the list.

First, I looked at fit. A cable pulls on the buds every time you move, so I looked for ear hooks, stabilizer wings, or cables that run over the ear. I favored pairs with an official IP rating over vague "sweat-resistant" claims. I also checked that each pair is sold with a plug that fits current phones, because a 3.5mm-to-USB-C adapter is one more thing that can come loose mid-run. Inline controls mattered as well, since a remote you can reach mid-set means you don't have to dig your phone out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that BYD’s new full-size electric SUV, the Denza N9 EV, was revealed in a regulatory filing, weighing in at over 8,200 lbs (3,760 kg). That creates one concern.

The Denza N9 first went on sale last March, a flagship plug-in hybrid (PHEV) SUV with a combined CLTC range of about 807 miles (1,300 km) on a full charge and full tank of gas.

BYD introduced the updated Flash Charging version earlier this year, which uses its second-generation Blade Batteries and delivers a pure electric CLTC range of 260 miles (420 km). Combined, it gets up to 944 miles (1,520 km) under CLTC conditions.

In the latest batch of new energy vehicles (NEVs) approved for sale by China’s MIIT (Ministry of Information Technology) this week, a new all-electric Denza N9 appeared.

The filing revealed the Denza N9 EV will be available with three electric motors, delivering a combined output of 1,193 horsepower (890 kW).

Industry observers note that A badge on the back reveals it will use BYD’s tri-motor e3 platform. The setup features a single 362 horsepower (270 kW) front motor and two 415 horsepower (310 kW) rear electric motors.

In a recent development, the electric version measures 5,270 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,830 mm tall, with a 3,125 mm wheelbase, which is the same as the current Denza N9 PHEV Flash Charging model. It will be available in five- and six-seat configurations.

While the filing reveals it will use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with cells from BYD’s battery unit, FinDreams, it does not provide specifics like capacity or driving range.

One relatively major thing to note: the Denza N9 EV has a gross weight of 3,760 kg, or about 8,289 lbs.

According to recent reports, obscene weight , and that applies to other SUVs as well. Vehicle registration taxes should be based on vehicle weight as it wears out roads and endangers other road users and infrastructure and wastes resources.

As AutoNext points out, this makes it too heavy for an EU category B driving license, which covers up to 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs).

Last year, the EU updated the rules, allowing drivers who have held a category B license for two years to drive alternative-fuelled vehicles with a maximum weight of up to 4,250 kg (9,369 lbs).

While the Denza N9 EV would qualify as listed, newer drivers would still need a commercial EU category C1 driving license to drive it.

It has been revealed that BYD launched its luxury sub-brand, Denza, in Europe and the UK in March, starting with the Z9 GT and the D9 van. More recently, it introduced the Bao 5 PHEV SUV and the Denza Z electric supercar.

#5724. Breaking: Germany’s EV share hits record 37% as BEVs beat gas and diesel combined

📅 04 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1216 w)
📖 Baca

Breaking: Germany’s EV share hits record 37% as BEVs beat gas and diesel combined

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1216 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority.
  • For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined.
  • Industry observers note that the overall market barely grew in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier.

For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.

Industry observers note that the overall market barely grew in October. Total latest car registrations rose 1.7% to 254,492 units, which means the EV growth came straight out of combustion cars.

Recent findings suggest that gasoline car registrations crashed 40.5% to 38,516 units, a 15.1% share. Diesel fell 21.6% to 23,882 units, or 9.4% of the market. Add them up and pure combustion cars made up just 24.5% of new registrations, 12.5 points less than BEVs alone.

Plug-in hybrids slipped 7.9% to 28,499 units (11.2%). So plug-ins accounted for about 48% of the German market last month, and the average CO2 emissions of new cars dropped 21.1% year-over-year to 79.4 g/km.

It has been revealed that as we reported this summer, BEVs became the most popular powertrain in Germany for the first time in June with a 28.4% share. They’ve kept climbing every month since: 32.4% in August, 34.5% in September, and now 37% in October.

In a recent development, through the first ten months of the year, Germany has registered 698,230 BEVs, up 60.7% year-over-year. That’s about 28.2% of the 2,476,290 upcoming cars registered in 2026 so far, up from roughly 19% for the full year 2025.

And the industry didn’t see it coming. In December, the VDA, Germany’s auto industry association, forecast about 693,000 BEV registrations for all of 2026. Germany passed that in October. At the current pace, it’s on track for somewhere around 875,000 by the end of the year.

Industry observers note that the biggest driver is Germany’s new EV incentive, which applies retroactively to cars registered since January 1. It pays €3,000 for a new BEV, bought or leased, and up to €6,000 for lower-income households with children. Households with taxable income above €80,000 (€90,000 with kids) don’t qualify.

The program targets private buyers, and that’s exactly where the KBA data shows the jump. Private registrations rose 20.6% in October, while commercial registrations fell 8.2%. Private buyers now make up 40.7% of the market.

In a recent development, germany has been here before. The government killed its previous EV incentive overnight in December 2023, and BEV sales fell off a cliff in 2024. This time, the money is going to the buyers who need it most, and it’s moving the needle fast.

In a recent development, tesla’s German numbers swing wildly with its quarterly delivery cycle. In September, the end of the quarter, it registered 12,552 cars (+268.7%) and the Model Y was the best-selling car in Germany. In October, it registered only 2,932, which is still up 290.9% but from a tiny base, for a 1.2% market share.

Recent findings suggest that year-to-date, Tesla is up 206.1% to 47,742 registrations. That’s a significant rebound from a terrible 2025, but BYD is now slightly ahead with 47,961 (+216.1%). BYD registered 5,173 cars in October (+54.3%), though the majority of its German sales are plug-in hybrids, not BEVs.

In a recent development, the other Chinese brands are growing even faster. Leapmotor registered 3,661 cars in October, up 288.6%, and is at 19,705 for the year. Xpeng was up 284.4% to 1,380 units, and SAIC’s MG was up 48.5% to 4,140.

According to recent reports, volkswagen Group still owns the top of the EV charts, though. Through September, the Skoda Elroq was Germany’s best-selling EV with 30,845 units, ahead of the Tesla Model Y (29,464) and the VW ID.3 (24,352).

The EV boom is happening during one of the worst years in the history of Germany’s auto industry.

Sources indicate that in October, the VW brand’s German registrations fell 4%, Audi dropped 8.4%, Porsche lost 5.7%, and Opel crashed 24.1%. BMW was flat (+0.1%), and Mercedes was the exception, up 8.5%. VW is still by far the biggest brand in Germany with an 18.2% share, but it’s down 5.6% for the year.

Last week, Volkswagen Group reported a €5.9 billion operating loss for the third quarter, its biggest quarterly loss since Dieselgate, driven by a writedown of its Porsche stake, weak sales in China, and thin EV margins. The group has already approved a initiative to cut 100,000 jobs and close several German plants. Mercedes cut its 2026 car margin guidance to 2-3% last week, mainly because of China.

Industry observers note that it’s not a product problem. VW’s upcoming ID. Polo is sold out with over 30,000 orders, BMW has over 50,000 orders for the Neue Klasse iX3, and the Elroq leads the German EV market.

Sources indicate that germany is proving what we’ve been saying for years. Give buyers EVs they can actually afford, and they switch fast. Fully electric cars went from about 19% of the market last year to 37% in October, and the country beat the industry’s full-year forecast with two months to spare. That’s not a slow transition.

One thing to consider when talking about EVs not being Germany-made is that Germany car makers can't make them fast enough. A lot of the models are sold out for months. It's not an excuse but something to keep in mind.

Industry observers note that compare that with North America, where EV sales dropped 44% after the US killed its federal EV tax credit. Same technology, sometimes the same cars. The difference is policy.

Recent findings suggest that germany’s problem is who’s capturing the demand. Hint: it’s not German automakers.

But whose fault is that? You can’t spend years dragging your feet on electrification and lobby government back and forth on EV incentives and then complain when those who are all-in on EVs are able to take better advantage of the customer shift amid another oil crisis.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Strive bought another 251 bitcoin last week for $17.5 million at an average of $69,853 per coin, Chairman and CEO Matthew Cole posted Monday, lifting total holdings to 43,404 BTC.

“Strive acquired 251 $BTC for $17.5M at an average cost of $69,853 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,404,” Cole wrote. A Monday 8-K filing reveals the purchases ran from Nov. 7 through Nov. 13, inclusive of fees and expenses, and took the Dallas firm’s stack up from 43,153 bitcoin a week earlier.

Recent findings suggest that cole stated Strive raised $10 million through its SATS at-the-market program. The filing puts that total at $10.02 million in gross proceeds from the sale of 104,478 shares of the manufacturer’s 15% Series A perpetual preferred stock.

Strive sold no Class A common shares and no shares of its variable-rate SATA preferred during the week. Cash and cash equivalents fell $22.3 million to $465.3 million as of Nov. 13. Cole also posted a preferred dividend coverage figure of 133 months and an amplification ratio of 76%, two metrics the 8-K does not break out.

The 251-coin add is larger than the 29 bitcoin Strive bought the prior week at an average of $75,721 and the 124 bitcoin it bought in late October at $80,526, but it remains a fraction of the October sprint that built the stack. Holdings stood at 28,000 bitcoin on Sept. 30 before Strive acquired 15,124 coins between Oct. 1 and Oct. 30, including a 6,182-coin buy.

Industry observers note that the tech giant closed a registered offering of 7 million SATS shares on Oct. 20 for about $609 million in net proceeds and later lined up a $1 billion SATS at-the-market program, the facilities that have funded the larger purchases. Effective common shares outstanding were unchanged at 127,331,109. SATS shares outstanding rose to 7,141,037, while SATA remained at 14,030,176.

Sources indicate that strive still holds 505,000 shares of Strategy’s variable-rate STRC preferred, marked at a fair value of $50.5 million as of Nov. 13. On Nov. 12, the board raised the regular dividend rate on SATA to 13.25% for periods beginning Dec. 1 and declared daily December cash dividends of $0.0502 a share on SATA and $0.0569 a share on SATS, which continues to carry a 15% rate. Those daily payments total $1.1044 a share on SATA and $1.2518 a share on SATS for the full month.

Strive’s Class A shares fell around 10% in Monday premarket trading to $19.34 as of 8:45 a.m. ET, from Friday’s close of $21.36. The move tracks a broader selloff in bitcoin-linked stocks. Strategy, the largest public corporate holder, was down 8.1% in premarket trading to $102.60 as of 8:45 a.m. ET, from Friday’s close of $111.62.

According to recent reports, ASST has already given back a large share of its October run. The stock closed Oct. 21 at $30.75 and Oct. 30 at $22.19. Monday’s premarket price is down about 13% from that October close and about 37% from the Oct. 21 close. The 52-week range runs from $7.02 to $32.08. Year to date, the shares are still higher: they finished 2025 at $14.76, leaving the premarket price up about 31% from year-end.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin traded near $64,300 as of 8:45 a.m. ET, after dropping below $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest level since July 14. A graphic Cole attached to his post valued the 43,404-coin treasury at about $2.99 billion, using a bitcoin price of $68,811 as of 4 p.m. ET on Nov. 13. At Monday morning’s spot, the same stack is worth roughly $2.79 billion.

Recent findings suggest that last week’s coins were purchased at $69,853, about 8% above the current price. Strive has not disclosed a companywide cost basis in Monday’s filing.

The open will test whether the weekly add can steady the stock after the weekend break in the bitcoin price, or whether treasury shares keep sliding as the cash session begins.

💡 Key Takeaways
